21	# TL;DR
22	
23	## Outcome
24	
25	Codex Dock must show current Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail state through one
26	relay-owned production truth path, and every freshness claim must be proven over
27	time from source change to rendered iPhone UI state.
28	
29	## Problem
30	
31	The app can look connected while the data is stale because liveness,
32	freshness, current-screen proof, relay state, Swift state, and test evidence are
33	not all bound to one contract. Static snapshots and route-health checks can
34	pass while the simulator still shows a stale or wrong Thread view.
35	
36	## Approach
37	
38	Make the relay the only owner of card truth, order, freshness, stream identity,
39	and heartbeat. Make Swift render that contract, reject stale compatible state,
40	rehydrate Thread Detail when relay recovery invalidates continuity, and expose a
41	canonical current-simulator UI dump command for what the app is showing right
42	now. Proof must be retained JSON/Markdown over time, not screenshots,
43	recordings, or one-shot fixtures.
44	
45	## 2026-06-02 Correction
46	
47	The previous `implemented` status was too broad. The relay stream and simulator
48	proof work are real, but the client can still get stuck while catching up, even
49	when the relay has current Codex data.
50	
51	This document is now the canonical client communication, refresh, and catch-up
52	reference. Section `0.6 2026-06-02 Client Communication And Catch-Up Audit`
53	supersedes later historical "implemented" language anywhere it conflicts.
54	
55	## Projection Supersession
56	
57	This live-update plan documents the already-built card-v2 implementation, but
58	the permanent projection identity architecture supersedes it wherever identity,
59	ordering, freshness, cache validity, proof truth, or phone-facing display DTOs
60	are involved.
61	
62	Canonical target:
63	
64	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_THREAD_DETAIL_OUTBOUND_DUPLICATE_ROOT_CAUSE_2026-06-01.md`
65	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md`
66	  `Proposed Projection Identity Contract`
67	
68	After projection cutover, Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail all use projection
69	`rows` keyed by `projectionID` with shared `snapshot` / `upsert` / `delete` /
70	`heartbeat` / `resyncRequired` semantics. The card-v2 `delta`,
71	`stateGeneration`, `baseSeq`, `upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`, and
72	`logicalHostID::threadID` vocabulary in this doc is pre-cutover implementation
73	history only. Raw `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and `thread/resume` are
74	relay-internal adapters or diagnostics, not production display routes.
75

288	## 0.6.3 Refresh And Catch-Up Paths
289	
290	The client has several distinct refresh paths. They need one shared law, but
291	today they are implemented separately.
292	
293	### Initial Load
294	
295	Dock and Archive:
296	
297	1. Open stream client.
298	2. Call subscribe route.
299	3. Load snapshot into `ThreadCardTable`.
300	4. Apply updates.
301	5. Resync if validation says the stream is no longer trustworthy.
302	
303	Thread Detail:
304	
305	1. Begin live buffer.
306	2. Start notification observer.
307	3. Call `thread/detail/subscribe`.
308	4. Replace ledger with snapshot.
309	5. Replay buffered notifications.
310	6. Render through `ThreadDetailScreenStore`.
311	
312	### Live Update
313	
314	Dock and Archive:
315	
316	1. Receive root stream notification.
317	2. Validate view params, epoch, and sequence.
318	3. Apply heartbeat, upsert, delete, or resync-required marker.
319	4. Project visible rows.
320	
321	Thread Detail:
322	
323	1. Receive `thread/detail/update`.
324	2. If buffering, append to `ThreadDetailLiveEventBuffer`.
325	3. If not buffering, apply update through `ThreadDetailDataEngine`.
326	4. Publish rendered events.
327	
328	### Relay-Requested Resync
329	
330	Dock and Archive:
331	
332	1. Relay sends `resyncRequired`.
333	2. Client calls `thread/list/resync` or `thread/archive/list/resync`.
334	3. Snapshot replaces table.
335	
336	Thread Detail:
337	
338	1. Relay sends `resyncRequired`.
339	2. Store calls `thread/detail/resync`.
340	3. Snapshot replaces data engine state.
341	4. Buffered live updates replay.
342	
343	### Client-Detected Gap
344	
345	Dock and Archive:
346	
347	1. `ThreadCardTable` detects the gap.
348	2. It returns a resync decision.
349	3. Lifecycle calls resync.
350	
351	Thread Detail today:
352	
353	1. `ThreadDetailDataEngine` detects epoch, sequence, schema, viewParamsKey,
354	   duplicate-source, or malformed-update problems.
355	2. `ThreadDetailStore.apply(notification:)` catches the error.
356	3. The detail view is marked stale.
357	4. The store does not always schedule a resync even when the session is still
358	   available.
359	
360	This is not good enough. Client-detected Thread Detail gaps must recover
361	through the same canonical resync path as relay-detected gaps.
362	
363	### Dock Row Invalidation
364	
365	When a Dock row for the selected thread advances, `DockView` calls
366	`ThreadDetailStore.sync(with:)`. The detail store treats that row change as
367	proof that the thread changed somewhere and schedules:
368	
369	- an immediate detail resync, and
370	- a settled resync after
371	  `CodexDockConstants.dockRowSettledRefreshDelaySeconds`.
372	
373	This is the right shape, but the recovery task behind it must be finite and
374	observable.
375	
376	### Foreground Resume
377	
378	Thread Detail has foreground work gating through `AppForegroundWorkGating`.
379	
380	Dock and Archive do not currently have the same gate on their stream clients.
381	That leaves room for root streams to time out, reconnect, or report state while
382	the app is still in a lifecycle transition.
383	
384	## 0.6.4 Confirmed Stuck Thread Detail Failure
385	
386	Short answer: yes, the client can look connected and still be stuck.
387	
388	Observed incident:
389	
390	- A live Codex session was emitting new assistant messages.
391	- The relay had current detail data.
392	- Dock rows could still advance.
393	- The open Thread Detail view did not show the new messages.
394	- App logs showed `thread/detail/resync` started and the relay responded
395	  quickly, but the client did not log a matching recovery finish/fail for a
396	  long period.
397	
398	Root cause pattern:
399	
400	1. `ThreadDetailStore.rehydrateAfterDockRowAdvance()` starts a recovery task.
401	2. The store begins buffering live detail notifications.
402	3. It calls `thread/detail/resync`.
403	4. The relay replies.
404	5. The store replaces the snapshot.
405	6. `replayBufferedLiveEvents()` drains the buffer.
406	7. During replay, `await apply(notification:)` yields the actor.
407	8. New live notifications can enter `handle(notification:)` while the actor is
408	   yielded.
409	9. Because buffering is still active, those new notifications append to the
410	   same buffer being replayed.
411	10. Replay can keep extending itself under live traffic.
412	11. `finishReplay()` may not run.
413	12. `recoveryTask` may remain non-nil.
414	13. Later Dock row refreshes are skipped because a recovery is already in
415	   progress.
416	14. The UI can continue to look `Live` because transport connectivity is not
417	   the same as screen catch-up completion.
418	
419	This is a client-side architectural weakness. It is not fixed by asking whether
420	the relay has current rows. The relay can have the rows and the client can
421	still fail to finish local catch-up.
422	
423	## 0.6.5 Additional Drift Points
424	
425	These are the other side doors and drift points found in the parallel audit.
426	
427	### Thread Detail Client Gap Handling
428	
429	`ThreadDetailDataEngine` can detect:
430	
431	- epoch mismatch,
432	- sequence gap,
433	- schema mismatch,
434	- view params mismatch,
435	- malformed update,
436	- duplicate source identity, and
437	- updates already covered by the current snapshot.
438	
439	But `ThreadDetailStore` does not consistently convert client-detected gaps into
440	`thread/detail/resync`. It can mark the screen stale instead. Stale UI is useful
441	as a visible fallback, but it is not a recovery strategy when the session and
442	relay are still available.
443	
444	Canonical requirement:
445	
446	- Relay-detected gaps and client-detected gaps use the same recovery path.
447	
448	### Root Stream Catch-Up Sequence Contract
449	
450	The relay catch-up window can send rows that are logically part of the same
451	snapshot generation, while Swift `ThreadCardTable` currently expects `upsert`
452	and `delete` updates to have `seq == currentSeq + 1`.
453	
454	Files involved:
455	
456	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`
457	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-subscriptions.mjs`
458	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`
459	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift`
460	
461	Risk:
462	
463	- If relay and Swift disagree on whether catch-up window rows advance sequence,
464	  the client can reject valid catch-up data and enter resync loops.
465	
466	Canonical requirement:
467	
468	- The relay and Swift table must share one sequence law for partial snapshots
469	  and catch-up windows, and tests must use the real relay shape.
470	
471	### Root Streams Lack Foreground Gate
472	
473	Thread Detail can wait for foreground readiness before reconnect work. Dock and
474	Archive root streams currently do not have that same gate.
475	
476	Risk:
477	
478	- Heartbeat timeouts, reconnects, or state updates can fire during
479	  background/resume transitions and create misleading freshness state.
480	
481	Canonical requirement:
482	
483	- Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail must share foreground/resume gating for
484	  network work that mutates visible freshness.
485	
486	### Connectivity Can Hide Lifecycle State
487	
488	`AppConnectivityStore` accepts lifecycle state and runtime connectivity state,
489	but runtime snapshots can overwrite the whole visible status.
490	
491	Risk:
492	
493	- The UI can say online/live while the app is actually backgrounded or
494	  resuming.
495	
496	Canonical requirement:
497	
498	- Lifecycle, transport, route diagnostics, and screen catch-up must be separate
499	  dimensions that combine into one displayed status. A generic runtime update
500	  must not erase lifecycle or route diagnostic truth.
501	
502	### Route Diagnostics Can Disappear
503	
504	System Health route diagnostics are not protected strongly enough from later
505	runtime connectivity events.
506	
507	Risk:
508	
509	- A route-level failure can be visible briefly and then disappear because a
510	  broader connectivity snapshot overwrote it.
511	
512	Canonical requirement:
513	
514	- Route diagnostics remain route diagnostics until replaced by newer route
515	  diagnostics or an explicit clear.
516	
517	### Host Routing Can Prefer A Degraded Endpoint
518	
519	Host identity resolution can treat degraded loaded state as good enough
520	compared with a healthy checking state.
521	
522	Risk:
523	
524	- A screen can stay pinned to a worse endpoint even when another configured
525	  endpoint is healthier.
526	
527	Canonical requirement:
528	
529	- Host routing should rank loaded-and-healthy above degraded, and tests must
530	  cover degraded-versus-healthy-loaded choices.
531	
532	### Archive Mutation Success Depends On Reconciliation
533	
534	The relay can perform an upstream archive/unarchive mutation, then fail during
535	post-mutation reconciliation.
536	
537	Risk:
538	
539	- The client may receive an error even though the upstream mutation succeeded,
540	  which confuses user-visible state and retry behavior.
541	
542	Canonical requirement:
543	
544	- Mutation success, mutation failure, and post-mutation reconciliation failure
545	  must be distinct outcomes.
546	
547	### Archive-Opened Detail Has Weaker Lifecycle Wiring
548	
549	Dock-opened Thread Detail and Archive-opened Thread Detail do not inject the
550	exact same lifecycle and connectivity dependencies.
551	
552	Risk:
553	
554	- The same detail screen can recover differently depending on whether it was
555	  opened from Dock or Archive.
556	
557	Canonical requirement:
558	
559	- Thread Detail is one screen contract. Its lifecycle, connectivity, and
560	  recovery dependencies must not depend on entry point.
561	
562	### Active Turn Recovery Is Passive
563	
564	The client stores active turn identity from command send paths, but recovery
565	when that identity becomes stale is passive.
566	
567	Risk:
568	
569	- Failed send, reconnect, or relay-side turn changes can leave the
570	  composer/session state out of sync with canonical detail rows.
571	
572	Canonical requirement:
573	
574	- Active turn identity must be reconciled from canonical relay detail/root
575	  state, not treated as a durable client guess.
576	
577	## 0.6.6 Target Client Recovery Law
578	
579	This is the intended architecture for all client refresh and catch-up paths.
580	
581	1. Transport connectivity is not freshness. A WebSocket can be connected while
582	   a screen is stale or catching up.
583	2. Every screen has an explicit state machine: `loading`, `live`, `catchingUp`,
584	   `stale`, `offline`, and `failed` or equivalent.
585	3. Every catch-up operation is finite by construction.
586	4. A resync snapshot defines a replay cutoff: epoch, sequence, and generation.
587	5. Buffered updates older than or equal to the snapshot are dropped.
588	6. Buffered updates newer than the snapshot are replayed once.
589	7. Updates arriving after replay starts do not extend the current replay
590	   forever. They either apply normally after the generation flips, or they enter
591	   the next generation.
592	8. There is one recovery owner per screen and host. Applying an update can
593	   return `needsResync`, but it should not recursively start hidden recovery.
594	9. Relay-detected and client-detected gaps use the same resync path.
595	10. Recovery tasks have a watchdog/timeout and a visible state.
596	11. New invalidations during recovery are coalesced into an explicit pending
597	    recovery bit, not silently dropped.
598	12. Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail share foreground gating for catch-up and
599	    reconnect work.
600	13. Connectivity display is layered: lifecycle plus transport plus route health
601	    plus screen catch-up.
602	14. UI displayed-state dumps are a first-class proof artifact.
603	
604	Net: the client should never be able to say `Live` unless the visible screen has
605	either applied current canonical relay data or is inside a bounded, visible
606	catch-up state.

882	# 1) Key Design Considerations (what matters most)
883	
884	## 1.1 Priorities (ranked)
885	
886	1. User-visible correctness: the top Dock row and open Thread view must reflect
887	   the newest provable state or explicitly show why they are stale.
888	2. Single source of truth: card facts and freshness come from relay stream
889	   contracts, not local reconstruction.
890	3. Fail-loud recovery: stale, corrupt, or unproven state must become visible
891	   and trigger rebuild/resync paths.
892	4. Realistic proof: source changes must be observed over time in the simulator
893	   UI and retained as data.
894	5. Small repo-native implementation: extend existing Makefile, Swift tests,
895	   Node tests, contract generation, and UI proof harnesses.
896	
897	## 1.2 Constraints
898	
899	- Mobile build/test/launch commands are Makefile-owned.
900	- Production timeouts, intervals, ports, and caps belong in
901	  `CodexDock/Configuration/CodexDockConstants.swift` or
902	  `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs`.
903	- Phone paths must not carry raw bearer tokens or OpenAI keys.
904	- The relay SQLite cache is a projection cache only; Codex/app-server history
905	  remains durable source history.
906	- The current worktree is dirty from adjacent work; this plan must not revert
907	  unrelated edits.

909	## 1.3 Architectural principles (rules we will enforce)
910	
911	- Extend the existing `dock/*` and `archive/*` stream contract instead of adding
912	  a second card-truth API.
913	- Add behavior-level proof at the route/state/UI boundary instead of broad
914	  repository policing.
915	- Keep current-screen inspection canonical and simple: one Makefile target, one
916	  JSON artifact, one short summary.
917	- Use code comments only at sharp contract boundaries such as heartbeat,
918	  generation rejection, and simulator UI dumping.
919	- Prefer hard cutover and deletes over compatibility shims.

923	- Closing Thread Detail downstream sockets on upstream recovery is blunt, but it

926	- Adding proof-result schemas is extra contract work, but it prevents proof
927	  reports from drifting into unauditable JSON blobs.

931	# 2) Problem Statement (existing architecture + why change)
932	
933	## 2.1 What exists today
934	
935	The relay materializes Dock and Archive card projections in SQLite and serves
936	`dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/subscribe`,
937	`archive/update`, and `archive/resync`. Swift consumes those streams through
938	`AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`, applies them in `ThreadCardTable`, and
939	renders through `DockStore`, `ArchiveStore`, and screen stores. Thread Detail
940	loads history with `thread/read`, paged `thread/turns/list`, then
941	`thread/resume`.
942	
943	The repo also has relay scenario proof, controlled simulator fixture proof, and
944	XCTest accessibility sampling through `CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests`.
945	
946	## 2.2 Original broken / missing behavior (concrete)
947	
948	- Relay schema and Swift understand `kind:"heartbeat"`, but production relay
949	  subscriptions do not emit periodic heartbeat updates.
950	- Swift applies compatible snapshots without rejecting older
951	  `stateGeneration` values.
952	- Relay upstream Thread Detail recovery can succeed invisibly, leaving the phone
953	  connected without forcing a rehydrate.
954	- `ThreadTurnsListParams` has no `itemsView`, so the detail path cannot require
955	  `itemsView:"full"` even though the proof script can.
956	- Live endpoint/source failures can be hidden by history completeness instead
957	  of failing the visible freshness state closed.
958	- Archive mutation scheduling exists but Archive convergence is not yet a
959	  first-class invariant equal to Dock convergence.
960	- Proof harnesses exist but are not fully schema-guarded, scheduled, or
961	  required for update-path changes.
962	- There is no repo-owned lightweight command to dump the current simulator Dock
963	  or Thread visual state on demand.
964	
965	## 2.3 Current implementation state
966	
967	The implemented architecture closes the original gaps:
968	
969	- Production relay subscriptions emit heartbeat updates for Dock and Archive.
970	- Swift stream application rejects stale compatible generations and uses one
971	  shared stream lifecycle for Dock and active Archive.
972	- Archive Cleanup no longer owns a cleanup-only Dock snapshot side door.
973	- Thread Detail requests full turn items on the visible detail path and
974	  rehydrates after relay upstream recovery closes the downstream phone socket.
975	- Live-source refresh failures make relay freshness stale/partial instead of
976	  publishing falsely fresh state.
977	- Proof reports are schema-checked and reject raw app-server `:4500` evidence,
978	  scripted stream side doors, mismatched proof run IDs, and missing route
979	  evidence.
980	- `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` dumps the current simulator screen as
981	  accessibility JSON/Markdown without relaunching, navigating, seeding, or
982	  taking screenshots.
983	- `rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof SIM='iPhone 17'` proves over-time
984	  convergence from controlled relay truth to visible simulator UI, including
985	  visible ordering.
986	
987	## 2.4 Constraints implied by the problem
988	
989	The fix cannot be a single Swift UI patch. It must bind the relay data contract,
990	Swift state model, Thread Detail session model, proof artifacts, and Makefile
991	entrypoints so a stale simulator cannot look "green" because only static or
992	diagnostic checks ran.

35	## 2026-06-01 Current Ask Answer
36	
37	The most elegant permanent solution is one relay-owned projection system for
38	every visible Codex Dock object. The system has one identity owner, one ordering
39	owner, one update ledger, one cache contract, one generated client contract, and
40	one proof witness source.
41	
42	The final architecture is:
43	
44	```text
45	raw Codex inputs
46	  -> relay source adapters
47	  -> pure projection engine
48	  -> versioned projection store
49	  -> projection view streams and witnesses
50	  -> Swift projection renderers
51	```
52	
53	No layer after the projection engine may answer "what visible row is this?"
54	again. Swift may render and validate. Proof may compare. SQLite may store. None
55	of them may derive production visible identity.
56	
57	This is the target pattern, not a narrow Thread Detail fix:
58	
59	1. One projection contract package defines the shared row envelope, snapshot
60	   envelope, update envelope, view parameters, typed payload schemas, and proof
61	   witness schemas.
62	2. The relay projection engine is the only production module allowed to create
63	   `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `rowRole`, `displayOrderKey`,
64	   `revision`, freshness, ledger operations, or diagnostic rows.
65	3. Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, Host Registry, Thread Detail, request rows,
66	   simulator UI proof, live-filter proof, sync audit, and fixture generation all
67	   consume that same projection package.
68	4. Raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live
69	   notifications, and server requests stay as relay-internal source adapters.
70	   They are never phone-facing display contracts and never proof truth.
71	5. The app receives projection snapshots and updates only. It keys visible rows
72	   by relay `projectionID`, applies `snapshot` / `upsert` / `delete` /
73	   `heartbeat` / `resyncRequired` by `epoch` and `seq`, and sorts by
74	   `displayOrderKey`.
75	6. SQLite stores materialized projection rows and view memberships under the
76	   projection contract version. A contract bump invalidates old materialized
77	   rows before they can be served as fresh.
78	7. Request cards are projection rows with request payload. `requestID` is only
79	   the JSON-RPC response-routing token; it is not visible identity.
80	8. Local metadata, pins, filters, host settings, previews, and accessibility IDs
81	   decorate or expose projection rows. They never create a second row set,
82	   order, freshness state, or identity namespace.
83	9. Acceptance proof compares simulator accessibility dumps to relay-emitted
84	   projection witness envelopes from the same run. It does not reconstruct
85	   expected IDs from raw Codex data or imported ID helpers.
86	10. CI enforces the contract with schema generation/checking, strict proof
87	    schemas, forbidden side-door checks, and live temporal tests that exercise
88	    snapshots, updates, reconnects, resyncs, request resolution, and cache
89	    invalidation.
90	
91	Net: the architecture makes identity bugs go away by removing every second
92	identity owner. If a visible row exists, its identity came from the relay
93	projection engine or the row is invalid.

234	## Architecture Decision
235	
236	The permanent answer is not "fix one duplicate." The permanent answer is a
237	single product projection plane:
238	
239	```text
240	raw Codex adapters -> relay projection engine -> versioned projection store -> view streams -> Swift renderers
241	```
242	
243	Only the relay projection engine answers these questions:
244	
245	- What visible thing is this?
246	- What is its stable identity?
247	- What source fact produced it?
248	- What order should it render in?
249	- Is it fresh, stale, partial, or diagnostic?
250	
251	Every production screen then consumes projection rows. Dock, Archive, Thread
252	Detail, request cards, simulator proof, and UI dump comparison all use the same
253	projection grammar. Raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`,
254	`thread/resume`, live notifications, and server requests become private input
255	adapters. They are not display contracts.
256	
257	This is intentionally zero-sunk-cost. If an existing route, DTO, SQLite table,
258	test fixture, or proof script lets another layer infer visible identity, it is
259	not preserved for convenience. It is deleted, quarantined as a non-production
260	diagnostic, or rewritten to consume projection rows.
261	
262	## Acceptance Standard
263	
264	The architecture is accepted only when all of these are true:
265	
266	- One schema source defines the shared projection envelope and typed view
267	  payloads.
268	- Node and Swift consume generated or schema-checked DTOs from that source.
269	- The relay has one pure projection engine for identity, source refs, order,
270	  freshness, and ledger operations.
271	- Dock and Archive cards are projection rows, not a separate `logicalHostID` /
272	  `host::thread` card grammar.
273	- Thread Detail messages and request cards are projection rows, not raw Codex
274	  rows normalized in Swift.
275	- Relay SQLite stores materialized projections keyed by projection contract
276	  version, source host, view membership, and projection identity.
277	- A projection contract version bump invalidates old materialized rows before
278	  they can be served as fresh.
279	- Swift display stores apply only projection snapshots and updates by
280	  `epoch`, `seq`, `projectionID`, and `displayOrderKey`.
281	- Swift never creates production visible IDs from raw Codex JSON, body text,
282	  timestamps, local UUIDs, WebSocket request IDs alone, or UI object lifetime.
283	- Proof scripts compare simulator accessibility state against relay projection
284	  snapshots or updates, not against a second reconstruction of raw Codex truth.
285	  Fields such as `expectedMessageEventIDs` are forbidden in acceptance proof
286	  outputs because they encode a second identity oracle.
287	- Test fixtures either come from the projection engine or validate against the
288	  projection schema. They do not invent production message/card IDs, and they
289	  do not compute expected UI IDs outside the relay-emitted projection ledger.
290	- Raw routes may exist only as relay-internal adapters, mutation routes, or
291	  named diagnostics. They cannot feed production display state or acceptance
292	  proof.
293	
294	Net: after implementation, identity drift is not a category of app bug because
295	there is no second production identity owner left.

297	## Zero-Sunk-Cost Permanent Solution
298	
299	The objectively clean architecture is a projection system, not a Thread Detail
300	fix.
301	
302	The relay owns a single projection contract package. Raw Codex facts enter that
303	package; versioned projection rows leave it. Every user-visible Dock object is
304	then just a row in a projection view.
305	
306	The architecture has seven laws:
307	
308	1. Raw Codex routes are adapters only.
309	   `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live
310	   notifications, and server requests may feed the relay, but they never define
311	   phone display identity.
312	2. One pure projection engine owns identity.
313	   The only production helpers that can create `sourceRef`, `projectionID`,
314	   `displayOrderKey`, row role, freshness, `identityVersion`, or
315	   `projectionEngineVersion` live in the relay projection contract package.
316	3. One ledger model owns updates.
317	   Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, Host Registry, and Thread Detail all use the
318	   same `snapshot`, `upsert`, `delete`, `heartbeat`, and `resyncRequired`
319	   semantics with `epoch`, `seq`, `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`, and
320	   `viewParamsKey`.
321	4. Swift is a renderer and validator.
322	   Swift decodes generated or schema-checked projection DTOs, validates the
323	   envelope, rejects gaps/mismatches, renders by `projectionID`, and sorts by
324	   `displayOrderKey`. It does not reconstruct visible identity from raw JSON,
325	   body text, timestamps, request IDs, UUIDs, or object lifetime.
326	5. `requestID` is never display identity.
327	   JSON-RPC `requestID` routes a response. If a request is visible, the visible
328	   row is still keyed by relay `projectionID`; request state is payload/revision.
329	6. Cache validity is part of the identity contract.
330	   Materialized rows are keyed by
331	   `schemaVersion + identityVersion + projectionEngineVersion + sourceHostID +
332	   view + viewParamsKey + projectionID`. A version bump cannot serve old rows as
333	   fresh.
334	7. Proof reads the emitted projection stream.
335	   Simulator/UI proof, live-filter proof, controlled fixtures, and acceptance
336	   reports compare the app only to relay-emitted projection snapshots/updates or
337	   a byte-for-byte retained witness export. They do not call `projectionIDFor*`
338	   helpers or reconstruct expected visible IDs beside the system under test.
339	
340	That is the elegance test. There can be many raw inputs and many screens, but
341	there is one place where a visible object becomes a visible object. If a future
342	feature cannot go through that place, the feature is architecturally incomplete.
343	
344	This deliberately rejects the cheaper alternatives:
345	
346	- no Swift-side duplicate suppression;
347	- no body-text dedupe;
348	- no "prefer newest route" heuristic;
349	- no second identity helper in tests;
350	- no keeping raw routes as hidden display proof paths;
351	- no accepting stale cache rows because they are "compatible enough."
352	
353	The end state is simple: the iPhone renders a projection view, and every row on
354	screen has exactly one relay projection identity.

356	## User-Visible Bug
357	
358	When an outbound user message is sent, Thread Detail can show that outbound
359	message twice.
360	
361	The intended behavior is simpler:
362	
363	- One user send produces one visible user-message row.
364	- That row may move or lose its live badge as canonical history catches up.
365	- It must not remain as both a live row and a canonical row.
366	
367	## Root Cause
368	
369	The original pre-projection Thread Detail path had no single canonical event
370	identity layer for "the same Codex item" across live notifications and
371	canonical history reads.
372	
373	That client path stored `ThreadEvent` rows in `ThreadEventIndex` and merged
374	only by:
375	
376	1. Exact `ThreadEvent.id`.
377	2. A secondary stream key of `turnID + itemID + kind + visibility`.
378	
379	That works only when every producer gives the same `turnID` and `itemID` in the
380	same place. The outbound path does not guarantee that.
381	
382	The dangerous path is:
383	
384	1. Thread Detail is live through `thread/resume`.
385	2. A user sends or otherwise creates a user message.
386	3. The live session can emit an `item/started` or `item/completed` notification.
387	4. The app turns that live notification into a `ThreadEvent`.
388	5. The Dock row updates, so Thread Detail does a canonical reread:
389	   `thread/read` + all pages of `thread/turns/list` + `thread/resume`.
390	6. That canonical reread is merged into the existing event index, not used as a
391	   replacement.
392	7. If the live row and canonical row do not normalize to the same event identity,
393	   both survive and render as two visible user-message cards.
394	
395	That was a client-side merge contract bug. The current work-in-progress moves
396	the direct Thread Detail display path toward relay projection DTOs, but the
397	broader architecture is not complete until all display surfaces and proof paths
398	share the same projection identity plane.
399	
400	## What This Is Not
401	
402	This does not look like a SwiftUI `ForEach` rendering duplicate. `ForEach` keys
403	rows by `ThreadEventRenderRow.id`, which is `event.id`.
404	
405	This does not look like an optimistic-send duplicate. `ThreadDetailStore.sendDraft`
406	does not add a local pending message row. It sends `turn/start` or `turn/steer`,
407	then clears the draft and updates `activeTurnID`.
408	
409	This does not look like a relay "sent the same command twice" bug from the code
410	path alone. The relay forwards `turn/start` and `turn/steer` to the active
411	upstream after checking that the downstream detail session is bound to the same
412	thread. It does not create Thread Detail rows.
413	
414	The duplicate is produced after the client accepts multiple representations of
415	the same logical Codex item and fails to collapse them.

564	## Why The Quick Fallback Fix Was Not Good Enough
565	
566	The reverted idea was to make `item/started` and `item/completed` use top-level
567	`params["itemId"]` when nested `item.id` is missing.

569	That may be part of the eventual fix, but by itself it is too narrow because it
570	does not establish a single rule for Thread Detail identity. It patches one
571	shape instead of defining the contract.
572	
573	The correct fix should define one canonical event identity function and route
574	all event producers through it:
575	
576	- stored turn item from `thread/turns/list`
577	- live streaming delta from `item/*/delta`
578	- live full item from `item/started` and `item/completed`

585	## Permanent Architecture Proposal
586	
587	The earlier narrow answer was "put Thread Detail row identity in the relay."
588	That is directionally right, but it is not the full permanent answer if the bar
589	is "this whole class of identity issues stops being a concern."
590	
591	The full answer is one relay-owned projection identity plane for every
592	user-visible Dock object:
593	
594	```text
595	raw Codex state -> relay projection engine -> versioned projection ledger -> Swift renderer
596	```
597	
598	Swift, UI proof scripts, simulator fixtures, and tests should never separately
599	decide what a visible production row/card "is." They can render, validate, and
600	compare projection rows, but they do not own production identity.
601	
602	This is a stronger architecture than a Thread Detail-only patch because the
603	same failure shape has already appeared in several forms:
604	
605	- Dock cards were ordered from stale thread-level metadata while newer turn
606	  state existed somewhere else.
607	- Thread Detail could merge live and canonical rows under different IDs.
608	- Request cards had their own card/request identity beside message rows.
609	- Proof scripts reconstructed expected UI IDs instead of reading the relay's
610	  display ledger.
611	- Tests used fake/static snapshots that did not exercise real temporal
612	  convergence.
613	
614	The permanent fix is therefore not "normalize one more payload field." The
615	permanent fix is to make visible identity, visible order, freshness, and update
616	continuity a single projection contract at the relay boundary.

717	### The Object Model
718	
719	Use three separate concepts everywhere. Mixing them is what creates duplicates:
720	
721	| Concept | Owner | Meaning | May change? |
722	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
723	| `sourceRef` | Relay normalizer | Stable reference to the raw Codex fact, including host/thread/turn/item/request identity. | No, unless the relay emits a supersession from pending to canonical. |
724	| `projectionID` | Relay normalizer | Stable visible row/card identity derived from `sourceRef` plus row role. | No. |
725	| `revision` | Relay ledger | Version of the content for the same `projectionID`. | Yes. |
726	
727	The renderer keys UI rows by `projectionID`. Content changes, streaming text,
728	request status changes, and canonical catch-up updates bump `revision`; they do
729	not create new row identity.
730	
731	The canonical identity namespace should include host identity, not just
732	`threadID`, so two relays or two Codex homes cannot collide:
733	
734	```text
735	host:<sourceHostID>/row:host
736	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
737	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/row:<rowRole>
738	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request
739	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/system:<systemKind>/<stableSourceSequence>
740	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/diagnostic:<stableHash>/row:unknown
741	```
742	
743	Dock and Archive use the same thread-card identity:
744	
745	```text
746	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
747	```
748	
749	The route `view` decides whether that row appears in Dock or Archive. Archive
750	state is payload state, not a separate card identity. The Dock/Archive card
751	`sourceRef` is:
752	
753	```text
754	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>
755	```
756	
757	The existing Dock `logicalHostID` field is a transition alias for
758	`sourceHostID`; if a payload
759	carries both and they disagree, the relay must diagnose or resync instead of
760	letting Swift choose.
761	
762	`sourceHostID` is the relay's canonical identity for the Codex source host. It
763	must be stable across Bonjour name changes, LAN/Tailscale endpoint changes, and
764	phone saved host config edits. UI labels can change; source identity cannot.
765	
766	The derivation rule is:
767	
768	1. Use non-empty `CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_ID` from relay-side configuration.
769	2. Else use the persisted value in `.codex-dock/source-host-id`.
770	3. Else create `.codex-dock/source-host-id` once as
771	   `local-<sha256(platform + user + CODEX_HOME + historyUrl)[0..12]>`.
772	
773	`sourceHostID` must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`. It must not be
774	derived from endpoint hostnames, Bonjour names, LAN IPs, Tailscale names, saved
775	phone host config, WebSocket connection IDs, relay process IDs, or
776	`CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_INSTANCE_ID`.
777	
778	### Projection Row Envelope
779	
780	Every user-visible projection row should share one envelope, even when the row
781	payload is typed differently for Dock cards, Archive cards, Thread Detail
782	messages, and request cards:
783	
784	```json
785	{
786	  "schemaVersion": 1,
787	  "identityVersion": 1,
788	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
789	  "view": "thread.detail",
790	  "threadID": "019e...",
791	  "projectionID": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1/row:userMessage",
792	  "sourceRef": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1",
793	  "rowRole": "userMessage",
794	  "revision": 7,
795	  "displayOrderKey": "9998239345599999|0000000000|9999999999|9999999999|...",
796	  "freshness": {
797	    "state": "fresh",
798	    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
799	  },
800	  "payload": {}
801	}
802	```
803	
804	The row-specific payload can stay typed:
805	
806	- Dock and Archive rows carry card fields.
807	- Thread Detail rows carry message/request/system fields.
808	- Request-backed rows carry `requestID` for responses, but the visible row key
809	  remains `projectionID`.
810	
811	The shared envelope is what kills identity drift. The screen can vary; the
812	identity and update rules do not.
813	
814	### Projection Snapshot And Update Envelope
815	
816	Each subscribed view should use the same stream grammar:
817	
818	```json
819	{
820	  "schemaVersion": 1,
821	  "identityVersion": 1,
822	  "view": "thread.detail",
823	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
824	  "threadID": "019e...",
825	  "epoch": "projection-...",
826	  "seq": 42,
827	  "scope": "thread",
828	  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
829	  "complete": true,
830	  "freshness": {
831	    "state": "fresh",
832	    "asOf": "2026-06-01T18:00:00.000Z",
833	    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
834	  },
835	  "rows": []
836	}
837	```
838	
839	Updates are only:
840	
841	- `snapshot`: replace the declared scope.
842	- `upsert`: insert or replace rows by `projectionID`.
843	- `delete`: remove rows by `projectionID`.
844	- `heartbeat`: prove continuity without changing rows.
845	- `resyncRequired`: declare continuity broken and force a replacement
846	  snapshot.
847	
848	Every update carries `epoch` and `seq`. Swift applies only the active epoch and
849	monotonic sequence. A new epoch without a snapshot is invalid. A sequence gap is
850	not "probably fine"; it is stale until resync succeeds.
851	
852	Every projection snapshot and update also carries `projectionEngineVersion`.
853	Clients store the active engine version with the active epoch. If an update
854	arrives with a different `projectionEngineVersion` inside the same epoch, the
855	client rejects it and requests the matching resync route. A new engine version
856	is accepted only through a replacement snapshot with a new epoch.
857	
858	`projectionEngineVersion` is required on every projection snapshot and update
859	envelope for Dock, Archive, Host Registry, and Thread Detail. Stored projection
860	rows also carry the engine version as cache metadata. If Swift sees an engine
861	version mismatch, it must not translate old rows locally; it marks the view
862	stale and asks the relay for a replacement snapshot.
863	
864	The existing route names can remain because they are understandable:
865	
866	- `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`
867	- `archive/subscribe`, `archive/update`, `archive/resync`
868	- `thread/detail/read`, `thread/detail/subscribe`, `thread/detail/update`,
869	  `thread/detail/resync`
870	
871	The elegant part is not a single generic route name. The elegant part is that
872	all three route families obey the same projection envelope and identity rules.
873	
874	### Cross-View Scope And Snapshot Authority
875	
876	Thread Detail already names `scope: "thread"` and optional `scope: "window"`.
877	Dock and Archive need the same explicit authority rule so card cutover does not
878	recreate merge ambiguity under new names.
879	
880	Accepted projection scopes:
881	
882	| View | Scope | Meaning | Snapshot replacement rule |
883	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
884	| `dock` | `view` | Complete active Dock view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local `dock` row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
885	| `archive` | `view` | Complete Archive view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local `archive` row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
886	| `archive.cleanup` | `view` | Complete Archive Cleanup candidate view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local cleanup candidate row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
887	| `dock` | `host` | Complete active Dock view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
888	| `archive` | `host` | Complete Archive view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
889	| `archive.cleanup` | `host` | Complete cleanup candidate view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only cleanup rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
890	| `dock` / `archive` / `archive.cleanup` | `window` | Bounded key range inside a card-like view. | Replace only rows whose `displayOrderKey` falls inside the declared window bounds. Missing bounds make the snapshot invalid. |
891	| `host.registry` | `view` | Complete host registry for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local host row for that registry view with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
892	| `thread.detail` | `thread` | Complete detail view for one thread. | Replace every local row for that `sourceHostID`, `threadID`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
893	| `thread.detail` | `window` | Bounded key range inside one thread. | Replace only rows whose `displayOrderKey` falls inside the declared window bounds. Missing bounds make the snapshot invalid. |
894	
895	Dock and Archive stream envelopes omit `threadID` at the snapshot/update
896	envelope level unless the update is explicitly scoped to one thread. Card rows
897	carry `payload.threadID` and, when useful for validation, an envelope
898	`threadID`. Swift must not infer a Dock/Archive snapshot's authority from the
899	presence or absence of row IDs; it uses `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`,
900	`viewParamsKey`, and window bounds.
901	
902	For every view:
903	
904	- `snapshot` with `scope: "view"` or `scope: "host"` is authoritative for its
905	  declared scope.
906	- `snapshot` with `scope: "window"` is authoritative only for the declared
907	  order-key range.
908	- `upsert` inserts or replaces exact `projectionID`s.
909	- `delete` removes exact `projectionID`s.
910	- `heartbeat` proves continuity only; it never changes membership.
911	- `resyncRequired` makes the active view stale until the matching resync route
912	  returns a replacement snapshot.

994	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
995	```
996	
997	Dock and Archive thread-card `displayOrderKey` is:
998	
999	```text
1000	<invertedActivityMillis>|<statusPriority>|<safeProjectionID>
1001	```
1002	
1003	Field rules:
1004	
1005	- `activityMillis` is the relay-proven newest activity time for the thread.
1006	- `invertedActivityMillis = 9999999999999999 - activityMillis`, left-padded to
1007	  16 decimal digits.
1008	- `statusPriority` is left-padded to 4 decimal digits and is relay-owned:
1009	  needs-approval/user-input before running before idle before error before
1010	  unknown/dormant when activity ties exactly.
1011	- `safeProjectionID` is the canonical escaped `projectionID` tie breaker.
1012	- Swift compares the full string only; it never parses it back into fields.
1013	
1014	Normative `statusPriority` values:
1015	
1016	| Card status | Priority |
1017	| --- | --- |
1018	| `needsInput` | `0000` |
1019	| `needsApproval` | `0000` |
1020	| `running` | `0001` |
1021	| `idle` | `0002` |
1022	| `error` | `0003` |
1023	| `unknown` | `0004` |
1024	| any unrecognized active status | `0004` |
1025	| `dormant` / not loaded | `0005` |

1073	### Host Projection Rows
1074	
1075	`host:<sourceHostID>/row:host` is a real projection row, not decorative
1076	metadata. It exists so host identity, labels, connectivity summaries, and proof
1077	state have the same identity law as thread cards and detail rows.
1078	
1079	Host row envelope:
1080	
1081	```json
1082	{
1083	  "schemaVersion": 1,
1084	  "identityVersion": 1,
1085	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
1086	  "view": "host.registry",
1087	  "projectionID": "host:amir-m5/row:host",
1088	  "sourceRef": "host:amir-m5",
1089	  "rowRole": "host",
1090	  "revision": 3,
1091	  "displayOrderKey": "host|amir-m5",
1092	  "freshness": {
1093	    "state": "fresh"
1094	  },
1095	  "payload": {
1096	    "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
1097	    "displayName": "Amir M5",
1098	    "endpointLabels": ["amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510"],
1099	    "connectivityState": "online",
1100	    "lastContactAt": "2026-06-01T19:50:00.000Z"
1101	  }
1102	}
1103	```
1104	
1105	Rules:
1106	
1107	- host rows are keyed only by `sourceHostID`.
1108	- endpoint, Bonjour, LAN, Tailscale, and saved-phone labels are payload labels,
1109	  never identity.
1110	- phone saved host configs are bootstrap connection records only. They may have
1111	  local config IDs for settings UI, but those IDs never appear in
1112	  `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`, or proof
1113	  witnesses.
1114	- host row ordering is stable label order unless a future host view defines a
1115	  relay-owned `displayOrderKey`.
1116	- thread-card rows reference the host row through `sourceHostID`; they do not
1117	  embed a second host identity namespace.
1118	
1119	Host Registry routes use the same projection grammar:
1120	
1121	- `host/registry/read`
1122	- `host/registry/subscribe`
1123	- `host/registry/update`
1124	- `host/registry/resync`
1125	
1126	`HostRegistrySnapshotDTO` and `HostRegistryUpdateDTO` are the same shared

1128	If the app shows configured endpoints before a relay connection exists, that is
1129	settings UI backed by phone config, not a projection view and not evidence of
1130	Codex source identity. Once connected, any user-visible Codex source identity,
1131	label, connectivity summary, or proof state comes from host projection rows.

1133	### Identity Law
1134	
1135	These are architectural laws, not implementation suggestions:
1136	
1137	1. No production visible row/card ID may be generated from body text, timestamp,
1138	   list offset alone, local UI state, Swift object lifetime, WebSocket request
1139	   ID alone, `UUID()`, or `crypto.randomUUID()`.
1140	2. A supported raw Codex item without enough identity does not become a normal
1141	   message row. It becomes a stable diagnostic row or a `resyncRequired` update.
1142	3. Live, history, reconnect, canonical reread, server request, request
1143	   resolution, and proof paths all call the same relay projection normalizer.
1144	4. Streaming and settled forms of one Codex item share one `projectionID`.
1145	5. Request controls are attached to the same `projectionID` as their visible
1146	   row. `requestID` is only the response routing key.
1147	6. Sorting is by relay `displayOrderKey` only. Swift does not rebuild newest
1148	   ordering from raw timestamps or turn/item indexes.
1149	7. Local metadata can decorate projection rows, but it cannot create production
1150	   rows or override projection identity/order/freshness.
1151	8. Diagnostics and health routes can explain state, but cannot be accepted as
1152	   data truth for the UI.
1153	9. Test fixtures must use projection DTOs or the relay normalizer. A fake that
1154	   invents message IDs is testing a different product.
1155	10. Proof scripts must compare UI state against relay projection snapshots or
1156	    updates, not against a second reconstruction of raw Codex truth.
1157	11. Acceptance proof cannot contain `expectedMessageEventIDs`, fixture-computed
1158	    visible IDs, or any other expected-ID list that was not emitted by the relay
1159	    projection ledger.
1160	12. Local metadata, including pin, hide, archive, and user filter state, may
1161	    request a relay view or decorate returned rows. It cannot change the row set
1162	    used by acceptance proof outside the relay projection view being proved.
1163	
1164	Pin and local metadata rule: cached pinned/local display snapshots are never
1165	authoritative after projection cutover. A pin can render chrome on an existing
1166	projection row, or a future relay-owned pinned view can be added with explicit
1167	`viewParamsKey` and witness proof. Swift cannot use local pin state to create a
1168	second row order, second membership set, or alternate cache of projection rows.
1169	
1170	### Relay Projection Engine
1171	
1172	The relay should have one pure projection engine that is independent from
1173	WebSockets, timers, SQLite, and Swift:
1174	
1175	```text
1176	normalizeRawCodexSource(rawSource, context) -> ProjectionRow[]
1177	applyProjectionOperation(ledger, operation) -> ledger
1178	projectDockView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<DockCard>
1179	projectArchiveView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<DockCard>
1180	projectHostRegistryView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<HostRow>
1181	projectThreadDetailView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<ThreadDetailRow>
1182	```
1183	
1184	That engine has one production module, not one module per screen. The target
1185	module is:
1186	
1187	```text
1188	scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs
1189	```
1190	
1191	All production helpers named like `projectionIDFor*`, `sourceRefFor*`,
1192	`displayOrderKeyFor*`, and row-role mappers live there or under that module's
1193	owned package directory. View-specific relay files such as Thread Detail
1194	ledger, Dock state, Archive state, Archive Cleanup, and simulator fixtures may
1195	call the engine; they must not define their own visible identity grammar. Tests
1196	may import the pure engine for unit coverage, but acceptance proof cannot use
1197	that import as its expected-ID oracle. Acceptance proof reads IDs from emitted
1198	projection envelopes only.
1199	
1200	Runtime code does I/O:
1201	
1202	- read raw app-server state.
1203	- maintain upstream live sessions.
1204	- receive server requests.
1205	- write/read SQLite projection state.
1206	- publish downstream JSON-RPC snapshots and updates.
1207	
1208	The projection engine does identity, role mapping, order keys, freshness, and
1209	ledger operations. It has no socket state and no UI state. That is what makes
1210	it testable and prevents "one more path" from becoming another identity owner.
1211	
1212	### Reference Architecture Components
1213	
1214	The clean permanent architecture has these components and only these
1215	responsibilities:
1216	
1217	| Component | Owns | Must not own |
1218	| --- | --- | --- |
1219	| Raw Codex adapters | Fetching and subscribing to raw upstream state: `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live notifications, server requests. | Visible identity, UI order, freshness labels, or Swift DTO shape. |
1220	| Source host identity provider | Stable `sourceHostID` for the Codex source. | Endpoint labels, relay process identity, phone host config, or display names. |
1221	| Projection engine | `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `rowRole`, `displayOrderKey`, freshness, diagnostics, and ledger operations. | WebSocket lifecycle, SQLite I/O, Swift rendering, or test-only shortcuts. |
1222	| Projection store | Materialized projection rows, view memberships, epochs, sequence numbers, and cache contract versions. | Raw Codex as durable truth or screen-specific identity grammars. |
1223	| View stream routers | `dock/*`, `archive/*`, `archive/cleanup/*`, `host/registry/*`, `thread/detail/*` snapshots, updates, heartbeats, and resyncs over JSON-RPC. | Recomputing row identity or order. |
1224	| Swift projection stores | Applying projection snapshots/updates and publishing render state. | Parsing raw Codex display rows, recovering missing identity, or fallback sorting. |
1225	| Phone saved host config | Bootstrap endpoint list used to connect to relays. | `sourceHostID`, `projectionID`, host row identity, or freshness proof. |
1226	| UI and automation | Rendering projection rows and exposing `projectionID`-based accessibility IDs. | Creating production row IDs. |
1227	| Proof tools | Comparing UI dumps to relay projection snapshots/updates. | Building a second raw Codex oracle for display identity. |
1228

1230	projection storage model:
1231	
1232	```text
1233	projection_contracts
1234	  sourceHostID
1235	  schemaVersion
1236	  identityVersion
1237	  projectionEngineVersion
1238	  createdAt
1239	
1240	projection_rows
1241	  sourceHostID
1242	  projectionID
1243	  sourceRef
1244	  rowRole
1245	  revision
1246	  displayOrderKey
1247	  freshness
1248	  payloadJSON
1249	  updatedAt
1250	
1251	projection_view_memberships
1252	  sourceHostID
1253	  view
1254	  scope
1255	  projectionID
1256	  membershipState
1257	  displayOrderKey
1258	
1259	projection_stream_epochs

1261	  view

1269	Dock active rows, Archive rows, and Thread Detail rows are all projection rows

1272	
1273	The existing SQLite `threads` table can be migrated into this model or replaced

1278	### Dock And Archive Migration Is Normative
1279	
1280	Dock and Archive are not allowed to stay on a parallel card stream grammar.
1281	They must move from the current card v2 stream to the shared projection stream.
1282	
1283	Current card v2 shape:
1284	
1285	```text
1286	kind: snapshot | delta | heartbeat
1287	id: <logicalHostID>::<threadID>
1288	logicalHostID
1289	stateGeneration
1290	cards / upsertCards / deleteCardIDs
1291	```
1292	
1293	Target projection shape:
1294	
1295	```text
1296	kind: snapshot | upsert | delete | heartbeat | resyncRequired
1297	projectionID: host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
1298	sourceHostID
1299	identityVersion
1300	projectionEngineVersion
1301	seq
1302	rows / projectionIDs
1303	```
1304	
1305	Normative mapping:
1306	
1307	| Current v2 field/concept | Target projection contract |
1308	| --- | --- |
1309	| `DockThreadCardDTO.id` | Removed as independent identity or transition-equal to `projectionID`; final identity is `projectionID`. |
1310	| `logicalHostID` | Payload alias only during migration; must validate one-to-one against `sourceHostID` and cannot appear in identity decisions. |
1311	| `delta` | Replaced by explicit `upsert` and `delete` operations. |
1312	| `upsertCards` | `rows` where each row has the shared projection envelope plus thread-card payload. |
1313	| `deleteCardIDs` | `projectionIDs`. |
1314	| `stateGeneration` | Removed; `epoch` and `seq` are the stream continuity contract. |
1315	| `baseSeq` | Removed unless the shared projection contract later adopts it for all views. Do not keep it Dock-only. |
1316	| `orderKey` | Replaced by `displayOrderKey`, opaque to Swift. |
1317	| `freshness.status` | Replaced by shared `freshness.state`; old names may exist only inside migration fixtures. |
1318	| archive membership | `projection_view_memberships`, not a second card identity. |

25	## Bottom Line
26	
27	The most elegant fix is not a Swift dedupe patch and not a broad rebuild. The
28	right architecture is to finish the relay-owned projection cutover that already
29	exists, make it the only identity path, and close every remaining side door
30	where the client, cache, proof, or tests can invent visible row identity.
31	
32	The permanent rule is:
33	
34	```text
35	If a visible row exists, its identity, order, and freshness came from the relay
36	projection engine, or the row is invalid.
37	```
38	
39	That rule kills the duplicate-message class by removing the second identity
40	owner. It also protects Dock, Archive, Thread Detail, request controls,
41	reconnect, cache reads, simulator proof, and live proof from drifting apart.
42	
43	## Model Consensus Result
44	
45	Model consensus converged on a finish-the-cutover plan.
46	
47	Both models agreed on these points:
48	
49	1. `scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs` must be the only production owner
50	   of `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`, `rowRole`, and freshness.
51	2. Swift should render and validate projection rows. It must not merge,
52	   identify, sort, or dedupe visible rows by body text, request ID, timestamp,
53	   thread ID, endpoint label, or local fixture ID.
54	3. Live Thread Detail and canonical history must produce the same
55	   `projectionID` for the same upstream item.
56	4. Proof must compare simulator-visible IDs to retained relay projection
57	   witnesses from the same run. It must not reconstruct expected IDs from raw
58	   Codex reads or local helper functions.
59	5. The remaining work is a strict cutover plus side-door removal, not a new
60	   optimistic/pending-message subsystem.
61	
62	The meaningful consensus correction to the earlier architecture doc is:
63	
64	```text
65	"One Swift projection table" means one shared apply law.
66	It does not require a giant generic rewrite if the same law can be enforced
67	cleanly through a shared core used by the existing engines.
68	```
69	
70	## Intended User Experience
71	
72	The user experience target is simple:
73	
74	1. The Dock shows the newest relevant work first.
75	2. Opening a thread shows the latest visible thread rows first.
76	3. Sending a message never creates duplicate visible rows.
77	4. Live updates, canonical history, reconnects, cache reads, and proof tooling
78	   all converge to the same visible rows.
79	5. If identity or freshness cannot be proven, the app shows an explicit stale,
80	   offline, error, or diagnostic state. It never silently guesses.
81	
82	The user should not need to understand Codex upstream notifications, relay
83	caches, request IDs, host aliases, or simulator proof internals to trust the
84	phone.
85	
86	## Final Architecture Shape
87	
88	The final architecture is:
89	
90	```text
91	raw Codex adapters
92	  -> relay projection engine
93	  -> projection cache/store keyed by sourceHostID + view + viewParamsKey + contractFingerprint
94	  -> projection streams: thread-card, thread-detail
95	  -> Swift projection appliers
96	  -> render-only SwiftUI
97	  -> retained relay witness proof
98	```
99	
100	There are only two display projection families:
101	
102	1. `thread-card`: Dock and Archive rows.
103	   The row identity is `host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard`.
104	   Dock and Archive are view memberships over that row family.
105	2. `thread-detail`: opened-thread rows.
106	   The row identity is
107	   `host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/row:<role>`.
108	   Request controls are payload on the projected row. `requestID` is response
109	   routing only, never visible row identity.
110	
111	`archive.cleanup`, `system.health`, and `host.registry` are not display
112	projection families for this plan. Current evidence shows they are local
113	filters, local status projections, or configuration. Turning them into streamed
114	projection views would add machinery without closing this identity bug class.
115	
116	## Non-Negotiable Laws
117	
118	### 1. One Identity Owner
119	
120	Only `scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs` may construct production
121	visible identity and order:
122	
123	- `sourceRef`
124	- `projectionID`
125	- `displayOrderKey`
126	- `rowRole`
127	- projection freshness
128	
129	Everything after that layer can carry, store, validate, render, or compare
130	those values. Nothing after that layer can derive them.
131	
132	Done means the repo has a gate that fails if production app code, proof code,
133	or fixtures build `host:.../row:...` IDs outside the projection engine package,
134	except in explicitly quarantined negative tests.
135	
136	### 2. One Stream Grammar
137	
138	Projection streams use only:
139	
140	- `snapshot`
141	- `upsert`
142	- `delete`
143	- `heartbeat`
144	- `resyncRequired`
145	
146	The stream is keyed by `epoch + seq` within:
147	
148	```text
149	sourceHostID + view + scope + viewParamsKey
150	```
151	
152	There is no production display `delta`, `card-v2`, `baseSeq`, `upsertCards`,
153	`deleteCardIDs`, or `transaction` grammar.
154	
155	### 3. One Client Apply Law
156	
157	Swift applies every visible projection stream with the same rule:
158	
159	1. Reject rows missing `sourceHostID`, `projectionID`, `sourceRef`,
160	   `displayOrderKey`, or `revision`.
161	2. Key rows by `projectionID`.
162	3. Sort rows by opaque relay `displayOrderKey`.
163	4. Apply same-row content changes by monotonic row `revision`.
164	5. Reject sequence gaps, mismatched `epoch`, mismatched `sourceHostID`,
165	   mismatched `viewParamsKey`, and duplicate rows.
166	6. Never merge by body text, request ID, turn/item fallback, date, timestamp,
167	   thread ID, endpoint label, local fixture ID, or accessibility ID.
168	7. Never optimistic-insert a visible row that the relay has not projected.
169	
170	This law can be implemented as one generic table, one shared apply-rule core,
171	or another small local abstraction. The architecture requires one law, not a
172	large rewrite for its own sake.
173	
174	### 4. Live Equals Canonical
175	
176	Live Thread Detail events and canonical history must hit the same relay
177	projection function and therefore produce the same `projectionID`.
178	
179	If the relay receives a live event without enough canonical identity, it emits
180	an explicit diagnostic row or requires resync. It never lets the client guess a
181	pending row and later dedupe it.
182	
183	### 5. Host Identity Comes From The Relay Handshake
184	
185	`initialize` must return the authoritative `sourceHostID` and projection
186	contract fingerprint. `relayInstanceID` is diagnostics only.
187	
188	The client must capture that handshake and reject or invalidate streams whose
189	`sourceHostID` or contract fingerprint does not match it.
190	
191	Endpoint labels, Bonjour names, Tailscale names, LAN addresses, and display
192	names are action-routing or UI labels. They are not durable visible row
193	identity.
194	
195	### 6. One Cache Contract
196	
197	The projection cache is valid only under:
198	
199	```text
200	contractFingerprint + sourceHostID + view + viewParamsKey
201	```
202	
203	When that fingerprint changes, old materialized projection rows are wiped or
204	made unreachable before they can be served as fresh. The cache may store rows,
205	but it may not derive identity.
206	
207	### 7. Proof Uses Retained Relay Witnesses
208	
209	Acceptance proof compares the simulator UI dump against retained relay
210	projection witnesses from the same proof run.
211	
212	The proof path must not:
213	
214	- read raw Codex as the expected UI oracle
215	- import local projection ID helpers as the expected UI oracle
216	- accept legacy proof keys by deny-list only
217	- allow arbitrary identity-shaped fields in witness rows
218	
219	## Side Doors To Close
220	
221	### 1. `initialize` Does Not Carry The Projection Identity Contract
222	
223	Current evidence:
224	
225	- `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` returns `relayInstanceID` on `initialize`.
226	- `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerMethods.swift` decodes `relayInstanceID`.
227	- The client does not receive authoritative `sourceHostID` plus projection
228	  contract fingerprint at handshake.
229	
230	Fix:
231	
232	- Add `sourceHostID` and `contractFingerprint` to `initialize`.
233	- Keep `relayInstanceID` only as diagnostics.
234	- Store the handshake in the host connector/session state.
235	- Reject or invalidate projection streams whose `sourceHostID` or fingerprint
236	  does not match the handshake.
237	
238	Done means the same Mac reached through two endpoint labels cannot create two
239	display identity namespaces.
240	
241	### 2. `logicalHostID` Keeps A Second Host Namespace Alive
242	
243	Current evidence:
244	
245	- `DockHostIdentityResolver` can fall back to configured host IDs.
246	- Some DTOs and local paths still carry `logicalHostID` style transition
247	  vocabulary.
248	
249	Fix:
250	
251	- Make `sourceHostID` the only durable namespace.
252	- Delete `logicalHostID` outright where practical.
253	- If a live migration risk is proven, allow one transition window where
254	  `logicalHostID` is a validated alias that must equal `sourceHostID`, then
255	  delete it.
256	- Demote `DockHostIdentityResolver` to action-routing, label, or migration
257	  helper only. It cannot define display identity.
258	
259	Done means visible row identity never depends on endpoint configuration.
260	
261	### 3. Dock And Archive Lack Row-Level `revision`
262	
263	Current evidence:
264	
265	- Thread Detail has per-row `revision`.
266	- Dock/Archive card streams and Swift card apply paths do not carry equivalent
267	  row-level revision.
268	
269	Fix:
270	
271	- Add `revision` to projected thread-card rows.
272	- Require it in the thread-card schema.
273	- Apply it in Swift with the same monotonic same-row update law as Thread
274	  Detail.
275	
276	Done means Dock/Archive and Thread Detail share the same update semantics.
277	
278	### 4. `viewParamsKey` Has More Than One Grammar
279	
280	Current evidence:
281	
282	- Thread Detail uses a canonical `sha256:` style key.
283	- Dock/Archive use plain strings such as `dock:<host>`.
284	
285	Fix:
286	
287	- Canonicalize every `viewParamsKey` through the projection engine.
288	- Use the same hash grammar for all views.
289	
290	Done means view identity cannot drift when parameters grow beyond simple host
291	labels.
292	
293	### 5. Projection Envelope Schemas Must Be Closed
294	
295	Current evidence:
296	
297	- Some projection envelope schema paths are closed.
298	- The model-consensus review still found schema-side risk around permissive
299	  envelope or witness objects and older docs treating this as incomplete.
300	
301	Fix:
302	
303	- Ensure every projection envelope schema has `additionalProperties: false` at
304	  every identity-bearing object boundary.
305	- Allow open payload bags only where the payload schema explicitly owns that
306	  openness.
307	
308	Done means new identity-shaped fields cannot silently pass schema validation.
309	
310	### 6. Projection Witness Schemas Must Be Closed
311	
312	Current evidence:
313	
314	- The witness path is the correct proof oracle.
315	- Witness schemas still allow arbitrary fields in places that can carry
316	  identity-like data.
317	
318	Fix:
319	
320	- Close witness envelopes and witness rows by allow-list.
321	- Permit opacity only inside payload areas that are not identity or order.
322	
323	Done means the proof oracle cannot smuggle a second identity vocabulary.
324	
325	### 7. Proof Reports Must Use Allow-Lists, Not Deny-Lists
326	
327	Current evidence:
328	
329	- Proof reports reject some legacy keys through deny-lists such as forbidden
330	  key names.
331	- A newly invented drift field could pass until code notices it.
332	
333	Fix:
334	
335	- Convert proof report schemas to closed allow-list objects.
336	- Keep deny-lists only as extra diagnostics, not the primary guard.
337	- Make route labels distinguish phone-facing relay routes from relay-internal
338	  raw upstream routes.
339	
340	Done means acceptance proof cannot pass through a new side-door field name.
341	
342	### 8. Tests And Fixtures Still Mint Projection IDs Locally
343	
344	Current evidence:
345	
346	- Some Swift test support and request-card tests build `projectionID` strings
347	  directly.
348	- Some legacy fixture normalizers preserve old event identity construction.
349	
350	Fix:
351	
352	- Generate test projection IDs through the same projection engine package or
353	  through engine-generated fixtures.
354	- Add a repo gate that fails on direct `host:.../row:...` ID construction
355	  outside the engine package and explicit negative-test fixtures.
356	
357	Done means tests cannot assert a shape that production no longer emits.
358	
359	## Explicitly Rejected Work
360	
361	These are not part of the permanent fix unless the product requirements change.
362	
363	1. Pending-row tables, `clientMutationID`, atomic `transaction` operations, and
364	   pending-to-canonical supersession machinery.
365	
366	   Reason: the current product does not optimistic-insert visible rows, and
367	   live Thread Detail already has canonical turn/item identity. Building a
368	   pending subsystem would add a second identity lifecycle to solve a problem
369	   this product does not currently have.
370	
371	2. New streamed projection views for `archive.cleanup`, `system.health`, and
372	   `host.registry`.
373	
374	   Reason: these are not current display identity drift sources. Archive
375	   cleanup is a local view over Dock/Archive rows. System health is local
376	   status projection. Host registry is configuration; host identity is solved
377	   by the `initialize` handshake.
378	
379	3. A universal `projection_rows` SQLite rewrite as a prerequisite.
380	
381	   Reason: the current cache can be valid if it stores relay-projected identity
382	   under the contract fingerprint. A universal store may be a cleanup, but it
383	   is not required to kill this bug class.
384	
385	4. Mandating a new generic `ProjectionTable<RowPayload>` or `ProjectionDTO.swift`
386	   shape.
387	
388	   Reason: the required architecture is one apply law. A generic table may be
389	   the cleanest implementation, but the plan should not smuggle in a rewrite if
390	   a small shared core enforces the same law better.
391	
392	5. Wholesale renaming of every "card" symbol.
393	
394	   Reason: names matter only where they preserve a second contract or mental
395	   model. The load-bearing fix is making old identity fields unrepresentable,
396	   not renaming working local symbols for vocabulary alone.
397	
398	6. Swift-side dedupe by body text, request ID, timestamp, turn/item fallback,
399	   latest date, or thread ID.
400	
401	   Reason: that treats one duplicate symptom after identity drift has already
402	   happened. The permanent fix prevents drift at the identity boundary.
403	
404	## Implementation Plan
405	
406	### Phase 1: Contract And Handshake Authority
407	
408	1. Add `sourceHostID` and `contractFingerprint` to the relay `initialize`
409	   result.
410	2. Add matching Swift decode fields.
411	3. Store handshake identity in the active host connection.
412	4. Make projection stream handlers validate `sourceHostID` and fingerprint
413	   against the handshake.
414	5. Keep `relayInstanceID` as diagnostics only.
415	
416	Verification:
417	
418	- Unit tests prove two endpoint labels for the same relay use one
419	  `sourceHostID`.
420	- Stream tests prove mismatched `sourceHostID` or fingerprint fails closed.
421	
422	### Phase 2: Uniform Projection Apply Law
423	
424	1. Add row `revision` to thread-card projection payloads.
425	2. Require `revision` in the thread-card schema.
426	3. Apply row `revision` in `ThreadCardTable` or a shared projection apply core.
427	4. Canonicalize `viewParamsKey` for Dock and Archive through the projection
428	   engine.
429	5. Consolidate the stream validation rules used by `ThreadCardTable` and
430	   Thread Detail so they cannot drift.
431	
432	Verification:
433	
434	- Tests cover stale card revisions, duplicate card rows, wrong
435	  `viewParamsKey`, wrong `sourceHostID`, sequence gaps, and resync.
436	- Thread Detail and thread-card tests assert the same law with different
437	  payloads.
438	
439	### Phase 3: Remove Host Namespace Side Doors
440	
441	1. Delete `logicalHostID` where possible.
442	2. If migration risk is proven, retain it only as a temporary alias that must
443	   equal `sourceHostID`.
444	3. Demote `DockHostIdentityResolver` to routing/label/migration helper.
445	4. Ensure local metadata keys are expressed in `sourceHostID` terms.
446	
447	Verification:
448	
449	- Same source host through Tailscale, Bonjour, LAN, or display name does not
450	  split pins, Dock rows, Archive rows, or Thread Detail rows.
451	
452	### Phase 4: Strict Witness And Proof Contracts
453	
454	1. Close all projection envelope identity objects.
455	2. Close witness envelope and row identity objects.
456	3. Convert proof report schemas from deny-list protection to allow-list
457	   protection.
458	4. Keep deny-list checks only as extra diagnostics.
459	5. Remove fixture-built expected projection IDs from acceptance proof.
460	
461	Verification:
462	
463	- Contract tests reject unknown identity fields.
464	- Proof report tests reject newly invented legacy-style fields, not only known
465	  bad field names.
466	- Simulator proof compares UI IDs to retained relay witnesses from the same
467	  run.
468	
469	### Phase 5: Test Fixture Quarantine
470	
471	1. Replace local projection-ID builders in Swift test support with
472	   engine-generated fixtures or imported engine helpers.
473	2. Add a repo gate for direct `host:.../row:...` construction outside the
474	   projection engine package and explicit negative-test fixtures.
475	3. Mark old fixture normalizers as legacy-only or delete them once tests move.
476	
477	Verification:
478	
479	- Test code cannot invent the same visible row identity production owns.
480	- Negative tests remain allowed only when they intentionally assert rejection.
481	
482	## Required Test Methodology
483	
484	The test methodology must exercise time, not just static snapshots.
485	
486	At minimum, implementation is not done until these pass:
487	
488	1. Relay engine determinism:
489	   the same raw Codex fact from history, live notification, reconnect, and
490	   resync produces the same `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, and `displayOrderKey`.
491	2. Thread Detail outbound convergence:
492	   send a message, receive live row data, resync canonical history, and assert
493	   one visible user row by `projectionID`.
494	3. Dock/Archive convergence:
495	   live card updates, canonical refresh, archive membership changes, and cache
496	   reads converge to one thread-card row identity.
497	4. Host identity convergence:
498	   the same relay reached by multiple endpoint labels produces one
499	   `sourceHostID` namespace and one visible row set.
500	5. Cache invalidation:
501	   changed contract fingerprint makes stale materialized rows unreachable
502	   before they can render as fresh.
503	6. Proof equality:
504	   simulator accessibility dump equals retained relay projection witnesses
505	   from the same proof run.
506	7. Negative contract tests:
507	   unknown identity fields, legacy proof fields, mismatched source hosts,
508	   mismatched fingerprints, stale revisions, sequence gaps, and fixture-built
509	   expected IDs fail.
510	
511	## Acceptance Definition
512	
513	This plan is complete when all of the following are true:
514	
515	1. Production visible row identity is constructed only in the relay projection
516	   engine package.
517	2. The `initialize` handshake gives the client authoritative `sourceHostID` and
518	   projection contract fingerprint.
519	3. Dock, Archive, and Thread Detail all apply `snapshot`, `upsert`, `delete`,
520	   `heartbeat`, and `resyncRequired` under the same identity, order, revision,
521	   host, view, and sequence law.
522	4. `requestID`, endpoint IDs, local host IDs, accessibility IDs, raw event IDs,
523	   timestamps, body text, and fixture IDs cannot become visible row identity.
524	5. Cache validity is tied to the projection contract fingerprint and
525	   `sourceHostID`.
526	6. Acceptance proof uses retained relay witnesses as the only expected UI
527	   oracle.
528	7. Schema and repo gates prevent new side doors, including test-only side
529	   doors.
530	8. The duplicate outbound-message scenario, live-before-canonical scenario,
531	   canonical-before-live scenario, reconnect scenario, stale-cache scenario,
532	   two-host scenario, and Dock/Archive membership scenario all pass through the
533	   real simulator path.
534	
535	Net: once this is implemented correctly, identity drift stops being a recurring
536	bug class because the system has only one place where visible identity can be
537	made.
