4	
5	Status: audit only. No product code was changed for this worklog.
6	
7	Target thread:
8	
9	```text
10	019e8833-0309-7b51-bd7b-05e2768e6533
11	```
12	
13	## Related Documents
14	
15	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_IDENTITY_DRIFT_ELIMINATION_PLAN_2026-06-02.md`
16	  is the current architecture plan for eliminating display identity drift as a
17	  bug class.
18	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_THREAD_DETAIL_OUTBOUND_DUPLICATE_ROOT_CAUSE_2026-06-01.md`
19	  is the duplicate outbound-message bug doc cross-linked by that plan.
20	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_LIVE_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_AND_TESTING_REFERENCE_2026-06-01.md`
21	  describes the expected live-update proof methodology.
22	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md`
23	  records the broader protocol/update history.
24	
25	## User Ask
26	
27	Audit what the app shows for thread
28	`019e8833-0309-7b51-bd7b-05e2768e6533` versus what is actually happening in
29	Codex. Do not fix anything.
30	
31	The audit was later sharpened to require an over-time comparison, not one static
32	snapshot. User also reported a physical phone crash after watching the thread
33	for roughly three minutes. Physical-device crash investigation was not performed
34	in this pass because the user separately instructed not to talk to the unplugged
35	physical iPhone 17 Pro path.
36	
37	## Short Answer
38	
39	The white Codex CLI updates in the user's screenshot are messages. They are
40	raw Codex `agentMessage` items and relay `message` rows, so they should appear
41	in Thread Detail when the `Messages` filter is selected. The gray italic
42	reasoning/status text is a different class of CLI-visible activity and is not
43	the same display expectation.
44	
45	The current "new messages are not showing" symptom is now root-caused to the
46	client Thread Detail refresh path. The relay had the newer rows and answered
47	`thread/detail/resync`, but the open simulator detail view started a refresh at
48	`2026-06-02 11:49:31.787` and never logged `refresh finished` or
49	`refresh failed`. After that, the app kept noticing dock row advances, but it
50	could not start another detail refresh because `recoveryTask` stayed non-nil.
51	
52	There is also a separate relay projection ordering bug for in-progress turns:
53	
54	```text
55	raw Codex emits completedAt: null for in-progress turns
56	relay timestamp parsing treats null as numeric 0
57	0 wins over startedAt
58	active rows get eventTime/activityTime null
59	active rows get the fallback max displayOrderKey
60	the Swift client trusts displayOrderKey exactly
61	```
62	
63	That ordering bug explains why active rows can appear in a confusing order. It
64	does not explain the later "no new messages are appearing" state by itself. The
65	missing-new-messages state is best explained by the client refresh/replay wedge
66	below.
67	
68	Correction after review: this audit was run on `Amir-M5`. The `local`
69	`127.0.0.1:4510` relay sample and the `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` relay
70	sample were two network routes to the same host. They are useful for proving
71	the simulator was seeing the source host, but they are not independent
72	cross-host evidence.
73	
74	The confusing part is real:
75	
76	1. The Dock card title is the long initial goal text, not a current-work summary.
77	2. The Thread Detail screen is on the `Messages` filter, so it hides the newest
78	   command/output rows even when those are the most recent actual activity.
79	3. The raw app-server `thread/read.updatedAt` is stale at the thread creation
80	   timestamp, while relay projection and raw `thread/turns/list` prove live
81	   activity.
82	4. The target parent thread has many subagent children and concurrent active
83	   turns, so "what is happening" is split across parent turns, child threads,
84	   command output, file-change rows, and agent messages.
85	5. The open detail screen can wedge its refresh replay under sustained live
86	   updates, which makes the screen stop applying new relay data even though the
87	   relay and raw Codex still have it.
88	6. The `home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` result is not a root-cause finding for
89	   this thread. It only confirms that this specific thread is an `Amir-M5`
90	   thread.
91	
92	Net: the app can fail in two different ways here. First, active-turn ordering is
93	wrong because relay projection loses timestamps for in-progress turns. Second,
94	and more importantly for the screenshot/current complaint, the Thread Detail
95	client can enter a refresh state that never completes, so later real messages
96	never reach the visible screen.
97	
98	## 2026-06-02 Stuck Refresh Proof
99	
100	Simulator app log:
101	
102	```text
103	/tmp/codex-client/thread-019e8833-log-20260602T175910Z/threaddetail.log
104	```
105	
106	The last successful Thread Detail refresh for the target thread finished at:
107	
108	```text
109	2026-06-02 11:49:30.901 ... thread detail dock row refresh finished ... events=2780
110	```
111	
112	The next refresh started at:
113	
114	```text
115	2026-06-02 11:49:31.787 ... thread detail dock row refresh started ...
116	```
117	
118	There is no later `thread detail dock row refresh finished` or
119	`thread detail dock row refresh failed` for this open detail view through at
120	least:
121	
122	```text
123	2026-06-02 12:59:02
124	```
125	
126	After `11:49:31.787`, the same log still contains repeated:
127	
128	```text
129	thread detail dock row advanced
130	thread detail dock row settle refresh queued
131	```
132	
133	That means the client was not blind to relay/dock activity. It saw activity,
134	queued more work, and then could not complete the already-running detail
135	refresh.
136	
137	## Relay Was Not Stuck
138	
139	Relay log evidence shows the matching `thread/detail/resync` request succeeded:
140	
141	```text
142	.codex-dock/logs/dock-relay.err.log
143	2026-06-02T16:49:32.158Z ... downstream.request_succeeded ... method=thread/detail/resync ... id=443 ... durationMs=322
144	```
145	
146	Central time conversion:
147	
148	```text
149	2026-06-02T16:49:32.158Z == 2026-06-02 11:49:32.158 America/Chicago
150	```
151	
152	That is the same refresh window as the simulator-side stuck refresh start at
153	`2026-06-02 11:49:31.787`. So the relay answered quickly. The failure is on the
154	client side after the refresh request begins, not a relay outage or a missing
155	relay response.
156	
157	## Client Replay Root Cause
158	
159	The wedged path is in:
160	
161	```text
162	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailLiveEventBuffer.swift
163	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift
164	```
165	
166	Relevant code:
167	
168	```text
169	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailLiveEventBuffer.swift:15 begin()
170	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailLiveEventBuffer.swift:27 append(notification:)
171	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailLiveEventBuffer.swift:31 takeBatch()
172	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailLiveEventBuffer.swift:40 finishReplay()
173	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:663 startDockRowRefreshIfNeeded(reason:)
174	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:688 rehydrateAfterDockRowAdvance(reason:)
175	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:697 replayBufferedLiveEvents()
176	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:706 recoveryTask cleanup
177	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:742 replayBufferedLiveEvents()
178	CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:754 handle(notification:)
179	```
180	
181	Plain-English flow:
182	
183	1. A dock-row advance starts canonical detail recovery.
184	2. `liveEventBuffer.begin()` turns buffering on.
185	3. The store awaits `session.threadDetailResync(...)`.
186	4. The store replaces local detail events with the canonical snapshot.
187	5. The store calls `replayBufferedLiveEvents()`.
188	6. Replay loops through `takeBatch()` until the buffer is empty.
189	7. `finishReplay()` only runs after that loop finishes.
190	8. `recoveryTask` only clears after replay finishes.
191	
192	The dangerous part is that replay awaits `apply(notification:)` for each
193	buffered event. Because `ThreadDetailStore` is an actor, those awaits allow new
194	live notifications to enter the actor while replay is still running. Since
195	`isBuffering` remains true until `finishReplay()`, those new notifications are
196	appended into the same buffer being drained.
197	
198	In a busy live thread, this can keep replenishing the buffer faster than replay
199	drains it. Then `takeBatch()` may never return nil, `finishReplay()` never runs,
200	the `refresh finished` log never appears, and `recoveryTask` never clears. That
201	matches the observed log exactly.
202	
203	## Why Tests Missed It
204	
205	Existing `ThreadDetailStoreTests` prove useful static and single-race behavior,
206	but they do not model this live traffic pattern.
207	
208	Relevant tests:
209	
210	```text
211	CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:46 testDockRowAdvanceRehydratesOpenThreadFromCanonicalHistory
212	CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:111 testDockRowAdvanceSchedulesSettledCanonicalHistoryRefresh
213	CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:177 testDockRowAdvanceDoesNotDropLiveAheadEventBeforeCanonicalHistorySettles
214	```
215	
216	The live-ahead test emits one buffered live event before canonical history
217	settles. It does not simulate sustained notifications arriving while
218	`replayBufferedLiveEvents()` is awaiting and draining batches.
219	
220	Missing coverage:
221	
222	1. No test proves `recoveryTask` clears under continuous live notifications.
223	2. No test proves replay has a bounded epoch or generation cutoff.
224	3. No test drives a long-running, busy, in-progress thread with repeated relay
225	   updates.
226	4. No end-to-end simulator proof compares visible Thread Detail output against
227	   raw Codex/relay truth over time.
228	
229	That is why this bug looked fine in tests but failed in the real Codex CLI
230	workflow: the app is mostly about live updates, while the relevant tests still
231	lean too heavily on small, finite update sequences.

563	## Confirmed Timestamp Bug
564	
565	The relay projector parses timestamps in
566	`scripts/dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs`.
567	
568	The bug starts here:
569	
570	```text
571	scripts/dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs:53
572	numberValue(null) returns 0 because Number(null) is 0
573	```
574	
575	Then in-progress turns hit this path:
576	
577	```text
578	scripts/dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs:548-555
579	turnCompletedAtMs checks turn.completedAt
580	raw Codex sends completedAt: null
581	turnCompletedAtMs becomes 0
582	```
583	
584	Then `itemActivityMs` treats `0` as present:
585	
586	```text
587	scripts/dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs:153-168
588	agentMessage uses turnCompletedAtMs ?? turnStartedAtMs ?? defaultMs
589	0 wins over the real turnStartedAtMs
590	```
591	
592	The local reproduction with raw Codex turn data produced:
593	
594	```text
595	turn.startedAt: 1780422101
596	turn.completedAt: null
597	turnStartedAtMs: 1780422101000
598	turnCompletedAtMs: 0
599	activity: 0
600	displayOrderKey head: 10000000000000000
601	```
602	
603	`scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs:21` also uses
604	`MAX_SORT_MS = 9_999_999_999_999_999`, which is above JavaScript's safe integer
605	range. JavaScript rounds it to `10000000000000000`, which explains the exact
606	fallback key prefix seen in relay output.
607	
608	The Swift client is not recovering from this because it is deliberately
609	contract-driven:
610	
611	```text
612	CodexDock/Models/ThreadEvent.swift:233-248
613	Thread Detail rows are ordered by relay displayOrderKey, then projectionID.
614	The client intentionally does not rebuild order from local timestamps.
615	```
616	
617	That client behavior is architecturally correct if the relay contract is
618	correct. Here the relay contract output is wrong for in-progress turns.
619	
620	## Earlier Simulator Evidence
621	
622	The app was running on the `iPhone 17` simulator:
623	
624	```text
625	simulator id: DEF1631B-7125-43C6-BFA3-4423BF103C91

627	```

630	
631	Dock screen evidence before opening the thread:
632

635	target row identifier: codexdock.dock.row.Amir-M5.019e8833-0309-7b51-bd7b-05e2768e6533

681	## Canonical UI Dump Harness Result
682	
683	Attempted command:
684	
685	```bash
686	SIM_UI_DUMP_DIR=/tmp/codex-client/thread-019e8833-detail-dump-20260602T162004Z EXPECTED_SCREEN=thread EXPECTED_THREAD_ID=019e8833-0309-7b51-bd7b-05e2768e6533 rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'

700	dump did produce useful on-screen text evidence.
701	
702	## Findings
703	
704	### Finding 1: The screenshot replies are messages.
705	
706	The exact Codex screenshot replies were found as raw `agentMessage` items and
707	relay `visibility: message` rows. They were not merely hidden command/tooling
708	output.
709	
710	Conclusion: those white Codex CLI updates should appear in Thread Detail when
711	the `Messages` filter is selected.
712	
713	### Finding 2: The current missing-new-messages symptom is client-side.
714	
715	The simulator app log shows a Thread Detail refresh started at
716	`2026-06-02 11:49:31.787` and then never logged `refresh finished` or
717	`refresh failed`. Later log lines show dock-row advances were still observed.
718	
719	Conclusion: the client saw new activity, but the open detail screen got stuck
720	inside refresh/replay and stopped applying it.
721	
722	### Finding 3: The relay had the data and answered the matching resync.
723	
724	The relay log shows `thread/detail/resync` request `id=443` succeeded at
725	`2026-06-02T16:49:32.158Z` with `durationMs=322`.
726	
727	Conclusion: this specific stuck refresh was not caused by the relay failing to
728	answer. The failure is after the client starts handling the refresh response.
729	
730	### Finding 4: Active-turn ordering is separately broken.
731	
732	Active turns with `completedAt: null` are projected with `activityTime: null`
733	and fallback max `displayOrderKey` values. The client then renders those bad
734	relay order keys exactly.
735	
736	Conclusion: even when the refresh path is not wedged, the app can still put the
737	wrong active-turn row at the top.
738	
739	### Finding 5: "Messages" can hide newest non-message activity, but that is not this whole bug.
740	
741	The most recent projection rows in earlier samples were command/output tooling
742	rows, while the visible simulator screen was on the `Messages` filter.
743	
744	Conclusion: the `Messages` filter can make the screen look less current, but it
745	does not explain white `agentMessage` rows failing to appear. The refresh wedge
746	does.
747	
748	### Finding 6: Raw `thread/read.updatedAt` is not trustworthy activity truth.
749	
750	Raw `thread/read.updatedAt` stayed equal to `createdAt` while raw turns and
751	relay projection rows changed.
752	
753	Conclusion: any client, test, proof, or diagnostic that uses raw
754	`thread/read.updatedAt` as current activity truth can lie.
755	
756	### Finding 7: The Dock card title is not activity-first.
757	
758	The Dock card title is the long initial goal text. It did not tell the user what
759	the currently active implementation slice was.
760	
761	Conclusion: even when a row is live and sorted near the top, its textual preview
762	can feel stale because the title is not a latest-activity summary.
763	
764	### Finding 8: Parent/child structure is not surfaced clearly enough.
765	
766	The target thread has 13 subagent child threads. The app header shows one root
767	thread with host/repo/status, but it does not make the parent/subagent structure
768	obvious.
769	
770	Conclusion: part of the "confusing mix" is real information architecture debt.
771	The app is showing a root thread, but the actual work is distributed across
772	parent turns and child threads.
773	
774	### Finding 9: The host evidence was narrower than first framed.
775	
776	The audit ran on `Amir-M5`. Therefore `local` and `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net`
777	were two routes to the same source host, not two independent host observations.
778	
779	Conclusion: the strong evidence is about the `Amir-M5` source-host path. The
780	`home` miss should not be treated as important root-cause evidence for this
781	thread.
782	
783	### Finding 10: The proof harness still has reliability debt.
784	
785	`rtk make sim-ui-dump` is the intended canonical "what is on screen" dump path,
786	but it stalled in this pass. Mobile MCP accessibility dumping worked.
787	
788	Conclusion: the plan to make simulator visual state dumpable is still
789	necessary. The intended proof path should be reliable enough that an audit does
790	not need manual Mobile MCP fallback.
791	
792	### Finding 11: Physical crash remains unverified.
793	
794	The user reported a physical phone crash after watching this thread for roughly
795	three minutes. This audit did not collect physical-device logs or crash reports.
796	
797	Conclusion: the crash is a separate unresolved fact. It should be investigated
798	with device logs/crash reports once physical-device access is allowed again.
799	
800	## Root Cause Framing
801	
802	This thread exposed both a client live-update bug and a relay ordering bug.
803	
804	The strongest root-cause framing after the full review is:
805	
806	```text
807	The relay had the new message rows and answered detail resync. The Swift Thread
808	Detail store then entered a refresh/replay path that can keep buffering new live
809	notifications while replay awaits notification application. Under sustained
810	traffic, the replay loop may never empty, so finishReplay never runs,
811	recoveryTask never clears, and later real messages never reach the open screen.
812	Separately, relay timestamp normalization makes active-turn row ordering wrong
813	because completedAt: null is treated as timestamp 0.
814	```
815	
816	The user-facing failure came from both a live-update correctness bug and
817	view-contract debt:
818	
819	- Client detail refresh/replay can wedge under sustained live traffic.
820	- Once wedged, `recoveryTask` blocks all later canonical detail refreshes.
821	- Relay active-turn rows had broken activity timestamps.
822	- Relay active-turn rows therefore had fallback max order keys.
823	- Swift intentionally trusted relay `displayOrderKey`.
824	- Multiple in-progress turns were flattened into one list.
825	- Dock card text is not current-work text.
826	- Thread Detail default visible filter is not "all latest activity."
827	- Raw thread metadata is stale.
828	- Parent/child live work is not explained in the UI.
829	- The canonical UI dump proof path is not reliable enough.
830	
831	The audit did not adequately prove the physical-phone path or the reported
832	physical crash. It also did not provide independent cross-host proof, because
833	the useful `local` and `Amir-M5` samples were both from `Amir-M5`.
834	
835	## Architecture Implication
836	
837	The existing
838	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_IDENTITY_DRIFT_ELIMINATION_PLAN_2026-06-02.md` is still the
839	right architecture direction for identity drift and duplicate rows: one
840	relay-owned projection identity, one client apply law, and retained relay
841	witness proof.
842	
843	This worklog adds one UX/proof requirement to evaluate during implementation:
844	
845	```text
846	The projection contract must make "latest visible row" and "latest actual
847	activity row" explicit, so the app cannot silently present a filtered message
848	view as if it were the whole live thread.
849	```
850	
851	That does not mean adding a new identity path. It means the existing projection
852	path should expose enough row visibility and activity metadata for the UI and
853	proof to say exactly what is being shown.
854	
855	## No Fixes Made
856	
857	This pass only read local Codex state, relay/raw data, simulator accessibility
858	state, and existing docs. It did not change product code, relay code, tests, or
859	runtime services.
860	
861	Post-review correction: the host framing was tightened because this audit was
862	run on `Amir-M5`, so `local` and `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net` were not
863	independent hosts.

1	---
2	title: Pinned unpin menu instability and degraded health on clean rebuild
3	date: 2026-06-02
4	status: root-cause-found
5	owners:
6	  - Codex
7	reviewers: []
8	related:

13	---
14	
15	# Pinned Unpin Menu And Degraded Health
16	
17	## TL;DR
18	
19	<!-- bugs:block:tldr -->
20	
21	Symptom: On Amir's physical iPhone 17 Pro after app startup, five pinned rows were visible. Two could be unpinned, then the remaining three were stuck. Swiping a pinned row no longer reliably exposed the `Unpin` action; sometimes the action appeared briefly and disappeared before it could be tapped. The same clean rebuild also showed partially connected health: Dock feed degraded, thread detail degraded, archive degraded, voice degraded, and diagnostics degraded.
22	
23	Impact: Pinned rows can become effectively impossible to unpin from the primary Dock UI, and the system health UI can report broad degradation even after relays were restarted, making it unclear whether the client is live, stale, or only partially connected.
24	
25	Most likely cause: two separate client-side problems. First, the pinned section is a custom `UICollectionView` bridge that calls `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update; live Dock updates or height/layout updates during a swipe can close UIKit swipe actions, matching the "menu pops in and out" symptom. Second, the health UI is treating a capped Dock row window (`Home: Showing 250 of 964`) as global service degradation, then applying that same fallback to Dock feed, thread detail, archive, voice, and diagnostics when no route evidence has been loaded.
26	
27	Next action: review the cross-linked architecture plan before implementing. Do not patch production code yet. The physical iPhone 17 Pro is explicitly out of scope for remote commands.
28	
29	Status: root cause found; fix not implemented.
30	
31	<!-- /bugs:block:tldr -->
32	
33	## Bug North Star
34	
35	The app should let a user unpin any visible pinned Dock row with a stable, tappable action. Live stream updates, route-health refreshes, layout recalculation, worker activity, or startup recovery should not make the swipe action disappear before the user can tap it.
36	
37	The health UI should distinguish "relay process is reachable but route proof is not yet available" from true degradation. A clean rebuild against restarted healthy relays should not show every major feature as degraded unless there is concrete route-level failure evidence.
38	
39	Architecture plan: [pinned-unpin-menu-and-degraded-health-architecture-plan-2026-06-02.md](./pinned-unpin-menu-and-degraded-health-architecture-plan-2026-06-02.md).
40	
41	## Scope And Constraints
42	
43	- Do not query, install to, launch on, log from, or otherwise control the physical iPhone 17 Pro during this investigation.
44	- Use source code, local relay diagnostics, logs, and the `iPhone 17` simulator for reproduction.
45	- Analyze first. Do not modify production code until the bug is fix-ready and Amir asks for the fix.
46	- Keep this document as the source of truth for evidence and decisions.
47	
48	## Evidence
49	
50	<!-- bugs:block:analysis -->
51	
52	### User-Reported Evidence
53	
54	- Physical iPhone 17 Pro cannot be remotely controlled for this diagnosis.
55	- After startup, five pinned rows were visible.
56	- Two pinned rows could be unpinned successfully.
57	- Three pinned rows remained stuck.
58	- Swiping a stuck pinned row does not reliably show the `Unpin` menu.
59	- Sometimes the `Unpin` menu appears and disappears before it can be tapped.
60	- Same app state reports partially connected health:
61	  - Dock feed degraded
62	  - Thread detail degraded
63	  - Archive degraded
64	  - Voice degraded
65	  - Diagnostics degraded
66	- This happened after a clean rebuild and relay restarts.
67	
68	### Current Repo/Runtime Baseline
69	
70	- Time captured: `2026-06-02T12:03:10Z`.
71	- Repo: `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client`.
72	- Branch commit at the time of investigation start was previously deployed as `e048b5d Unify Dock projection identity`.
73	- The first diagnostic pass used source reads only and avoided all physical-device commands after Amir unplugged the iPhone 17 Pro.
74	
75	### Runtime Evidence: Relay Health Was Not The Broad Failure
76	
77	Relay route summaries were collected from both configured hosts:
78	
79	- `http://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
80	- `http://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
81	
82	Both relays returned `/syncz` as:
83	
84	```json
85	{"ok":true,"service":"codex-dock-relay","schema":"codexdock.syncz.v1","state":"available"}
86	```
87	
88	The route summaries did not show app-critical failures. They showed a mix of healthy exercised routes and unknown passive/manual routes:
89	
90	- `dock/resync`, `dock/subscribe`, and `initialize` had healthy evidence on at least the local host path.
91	- `dock/update`, `thread/detail/*`, archive mutation/update routes, and voice routes were mostly `unknown` because they are passive/manual routes and had not been exercised.
92	- `appCriticalFailures` was `[]` on both hosts.
93	
94	Inference: the relays were reachable. Unknown route evidence exists, but that is not the same as a failed relay. The user-visible "everything degraded" screen needed client-side explanation.
95	
96	### Simulator Evidence: Health Degradation Is A Dock Window Fallback
97	
98	The `iPhone 17` simulator was launched with:
99	
100	```bash
101	FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
102	```
103	
104	Accessibility dump evidence from the Dock screen:
105	
106	- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
107	  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=0; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; 487 shown ... Partial`
108	- `codexdock.connectivity.global` label:
109	  - `Online 2/2`
110	- `codexdock.connectivity.global` value:
111	  - `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`
112	
113	After opening System Health from the global indicator, accessibility showed:
114	
115	- Summary:
116	  - `Partial`
117	  - `Home: Showing 250 of 964`
118	- `codexdock.system-health.category.dockFeed`:
119	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
120	- `codexdock.system-health.category.threadDetail`:
121	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
122	- `codexdock.system-health.category.archive`:
123	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
124	- `codexdock.system-health.category.voice`:
125	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
126	- `codexdock.system-health.category.diagnostics`:
127	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
128	
129	Opening the `Home` host detail showed:
130	
131	- `State, Showing 250 of 964`
132	- `Technical Evidence`
133	- `No route evidence yet.`
134	
135	Conclusion: the System Health screen degraded every category without route-level evidence. It copied the global Dock row-window partial message into unrelated feature categories.
136	
137	### Code Anchor: Dock Row Windows Become Connectivity Partial
138	
139	The row-window state originates in `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`.
140	
141	Relevant source anchors:
142	
143	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:428-435`: if a stream snapshot is not complete, `hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: visibleRows, message: "Showing \(visibleRows) of \(knownTotal)")`.
144	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:364`: `DockRenderInput.isPartial` becomes true if any host is checking or partial.
145	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:278-296`: loaded Dock snapshots are reported to `AppConnectivityStore`.
146	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:419-437`: `.partial(_, message)` Dock host status becomes `HostConnectivityPhase.partial(message)`.
147	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:610-616`: if all hosts are online-like but at least one is partial, the global status becomes `.partial("\(host): \(message)")`.
148	
149	This means `Home: Showing 250 of 964` is currently treated as global connectivity partiality even though it is actually a data-window completeness fact.
150	
151	### Code Anchor: System Health Falls Back From Global Partial To Every Category
152	
153	Relevant source anchors:
154	
155	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:66-68`: System Health projects from `store.hosts` and `store.overallStatus`.
156	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:50-57`: route diagnostics are only fetched by tapping `Run check`; they are not fetched on open.
157	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:31-35`: if a category has no route diagnostics, it uses `fallbackStatus(for:overallStatus:)`.
158	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:78-79`: global `.partial(message)` maps to category `.degraded(message, nextAction: "Run check or open host details.")`.
159	
160	This is the exact code path that reproduced in the simulator: the `Home` row-window partial became a global `.partial`, then every category with no route evidence displayed `Degraded`.
161	
162	### Code Anchor: Pinned Rows Are A Custom UIKit Collection View
163	
164	Pinned rows do not use the normal SwiftUI `DockSwipeActionRow` path. In `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`, body rows use `dockRow(row, resetToken:)`, but pinned rows use `dockPinnedRow(row)` inside `DockPinnedSectionView`.
165	
166	Relevant source anchors:
167	
168	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:729`: renders `DockPinnedSectionView` when `projection.pinnedRows` is not empty.
169	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:733`: pinned reorder callback calls `Task { await store.reorderPinnedRows(rows) }`.
170	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:734`: pinned unpin callback calls `Task { await store.setPinned(false, for: row) }`.
171	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:859`: `dockPinnedRow(_:)` renders only `dockRowContent`, with `showsContextMenu: false`.
172	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:219`: pinned rows render through `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView`.
173	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:274`: `makeUIView` creates a `UICollectionView`.
174	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:279`: trailing swipe actions are provided by `UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration.trailingSwipeActionsConfigurationProvider`.
175	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:310`: `updateUIView` runs on SwiftUI updates.
176	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:315-320`: when not moving, `updateUIView` assigns `workingRows = rows`, calls `collectionView.reloadData()`, invalidates layout, forces layout, and reports measured height.
177	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:425-428`: the `Unpin` contextual action calls `parent.onUnpin(row)` and completes.
178	
179	First inference: any SwiftUI update to the pinned section while a UIKit trailing swipe action is open can cause `reloadData()`. UIKit list reloads close open swipe actions. This matches the user-visible symptom where the menu appears briefly and disappears.
180	
181	### Code Anchor: Body Rows Use A Separate Swipe Implementation
182	
183	Body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`, a SwiftUI view with local `offset` state.
184	
185	Relevant source anchors:
186	
187	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:8`: `DockSwipeActionRow`.
188	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:16`: local `@State private var offset`.
189	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:30`: `.simultaneousGesture(dragGesture)`.
190	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:42-50`: row ID, pin state, and render revision changes close the action.
191	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:832`: body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`.
192	
193	First inference: pinned rows and body rows use materially different interaction implementations. A bug in pinned unpin can exist even if body row pin/unpin behaves normally.
194	
195	### Code Anchor: Pin/Unpin Is Local Metadata
196	
197	Relevant source anchors:
198	
199	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:208`: `setPinned(_:for:)`.
200	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:209-215`: pin/unpin persists through `persistMetadataChange`.
201	- `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift:93-100`: setting pinned updates `pinnedAt` and `pinnedOrder`; unpin clears both.
202	
203	First inference: the stuck swipe menu is likely an interaction/rendering issue before the `setPinned(false, for:)` action fires. The user's report says the menu often cannot be tapped; that is different from tapping `Unpin` and having persistence fail.
204	
205	### Simulator Evidence: Five Pinned Rows Survive Startup
206	
207	The simulator initially had no metadata file:
208	
209	- App container: `.../Library/Application Support/CodexDock`
210	- `thread-metadata.json`: absent
211	
212	To approximate the physical-phone startup state without touching the physical phone, five current `Amir-M5` Dock rows were seeded into the simulator's own app data as pinned local metadata. Each entry used the real app key shape:
213	
214	- `hostID`
215	- `backendSessionID`
216	- `threadID`
217	- `isPinned`
218	- `pinnedAt`
219	- `pinnedOrder`
220	
221	After relaunching with:
222	
223	```bash
224	FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
225	```
226	
227	Accessibility showed:
228	
229	- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
230	  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=5; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; ... Partial`
231	- `codexdock.dock.pinned.toggle` value:
232	  - `Expanded, Pinned 5`
233	- `codexdock.dock.pinned.header` text:
234	  - `Pinned 5`
235	
236	Conclusion: persisted local pin metadata is loaded and projected correctly after startup in the simulator. The remaining bug is not "pins vanish on restart"; it is the pinned interaction surface becoming unstable after pins are present.
237	
238	### Simulator Evidence: Pinned Section Accessibility Shape Is Suspicious
239	
240	With five pins seeded, the accessibility tree showed:
241	
242	- Pinned header at `y=303`.
243	- Only one visible pinned row element was exposed at `y=782`.
244	- That row had value ending in `Pinned`.
245	
246	This does not by itself prove a layout bug, because accessibility listing only reports visible elements and the embedded collection is tall. But it reinforces that the pinned section is a large embedded UIKit surface with its own cell layout, not the same simple SwiftUI row stack used by body rows.
247	
248	### Testing Tool Drift: `sim-ui-dump` Contract Is Not Trustworthy Right Now
249	
250	Before seeded pins, `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` produced useful files but exited nonzero because the proof schema rejected the dump:
251	
252	```text
253	proof report contract check failed: /tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json/app: must NOT have additional properties
254	```
255	
256	This means the simulator dump producer and `contract/proof/sim-ui-dump.schema.json` have drifted. The dump still wrote:
257	
258	- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json`
259	- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.md`
260	
261	After seeding five pinned rows, a second `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` hung during the current visible screen XCTest path and had to be killed. The lower-level Mobile MCP accessibility dump still worked and captured the pinned state. This is relevant because the formal proof path is currently weak around exactly the UI state under investigation.
262	
263	## Investigation Log
264	
265	### 2026-06-02T12:03Z Initial Source Triage
266	
267	Actions:
268	
269	- Confirmed active goal and physical iPhone 17 Pro no-touch constraint.
270	- Searched source for `pin`, `pinned`, `unpin`, `swipeActions`, `contextMenu`, degraded health, and route-health terms.
271	- Read `DockPinnedViews.swift`, `DockView.swift`, `DockStore.swift`, and `DockCardProjection.swift`.
272	
273	Learned:
274	
275	- Pinned rows are implemented as a custom UIKit `UICollectionView` list with trailing swipe actions and long-press reorder.
276	- Pinned rows call `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update when not actively moving.
277	- Body rows use a separate SwiftUI offset-based swipe row and are not equivalent to pinned rows.
278	- Pinned row content intentionally disables the normal context menu.
279	- Unpin persistence is local metadata; the observed failure is probably before persistence because the action cannot be stably tapped.
280	
281	### 2026-06-02T12:07Z Relay And Health Evidence
282	
283	Actions:
284	
285	- Queried local and home relay health endpoints.
286	- Opened System Health in the `iPhone 17` simulator through accessibility, not screenshots.
287	- Opened `Home` host detail inside System Health.
288	- Read `ThreadCardTable`, `AppConnectivityStore`, `SystemHealthView`, and `SystemHealthProjector`.
289	
290	Learned:
291	
292	- Relays were reachable and `/syncz` returned `state=available`.
293	- The simulator global indicator showed `Online 2/2`, but value `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
294	- System Health showed every category degraded for the same reason: `Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
295	- The `Home` host detail said `No route evidence yet.`
296	- Code confirms route diagnostics are not auto-fetched when System Health opens; the `Run check` button is the fetch path.
297	- Code confirms global `.partial` falls back to category `.degraded` when a category has no route evidence.
298	
299	Conclusion:
300	
301	The broad degraded UI is a client classification bug. A capped Dock row window is being presented as feature degradation across unrelated categories.
302	
303	### 2026-06-02T12:11Z Simulator Pinned-State Reproduction
304	
305	Actions:
306	
307	- Confirmed simulator app data had no existing `thread-metadata.json`.
308	- Fetched current Dock cards from the relay card stream to avoid guessing metadata keys.
309	- Seeded five simulator-only local metadata pins using real `hostID/backendSessionID/threadID` keys.
310	- Relaunched the app with `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'`.
311	- Dumped visible simulator accessibility via Mobile MCP against the simulator UDID.
312	
313	Learned:
314	
315	- The simulator Dock loaded with `pinned=5`.
316	- The pinned header displayed `Pinned 5`.
317	- At least one pinned row was visible and carried accessibility value `Pinned`.
318	- Pin persistence and projection survived restart.
319	
320	Conclusion:
321	
322	The remaining pinned problem is focused on the interaction layer: exposing and tapping `Unpin` on pinned rows.
323	
324	### 2026-06-02T12:13Z Formal UI Dump Gap
325	
326	Actions:
327	
328	- Ran `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` after seeded pins.
329	- Stopped the dump after it hung.
330	
331	Learned:
332	
333	- The first dump before seeded pins already revealed schema drift: top-level `app` exists in produced JSON but is rejected by the proof schema.
334	- The second dump hung in `CodexDockCurrentUIDumpTests/testDumpsCurrentVisibleScreenOnce`; only config was written under `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T121309Z/`.
335	- Mobile MCP accessibility dumping still worked.
336	
337	Conclusion:
338	
339	Our simulator proof path has blind spots in this class of bug. It can fail schema validation or hang in the precise pinned/high-text accessibility state we need to diagnose.
340	
341	## Ranked Hypotheses
342	
343	### H1: Pinned UIKit `reloadData()` closes swipe actions during live updates
344	
345	Confidence: high after source triage plus simulator pinned-state reproduction; not yet instrumented with a swipe-open timestamp.
346	
347	Mechanism:
348	
349	- User swipes a pinned row.
350	- UIKit opens the trailing `Unpin` action.
351	- A live Dock update, projection revision, health state update, height measurement callback, or other SwiftUI state change re-runs `updateUIView`.
352	- `updateUIView` calls `collectionView.reloadData()`.
353	- UIKit closes the open swipe action.
354	- User sees the menu pop in and out before it can be tapped.
355	
356	Why it fits:
357	
358	- The symptom is instability of the menu, not a failed `Unpin` action after tap.
359	- It can be worse after startup, when streams/health/status updates are still settling.
360	- It can be worse with live work happening, because updates keep arriving.
361	- It is specific to pinned rows because pinned rows use a collection view bridge.
362	
363	What would prove it:
364	
365	- Simulator reproduction where opening a pinned-row swipe action followed by a live Dock update or forced render update closes the action.
366	- Logs/instrumentation showing `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView.updateUIView`/`reloadData()` happens while the swipe action is open.
367	- A UI dump or XCTest proof showing `Unpin` action appears and disappears across samples without user tapping it.
368	
369	Current evidence:
370	
371	- The exact code path calls `collectionView.reloadData()` on every `updateUIView` while not moving.
372	- The simulator reproduced the same five-pinned startup state.
373	- The app is live and continuously receiving Dock stream/health changes.
374	- UIKit list reloads are known to close active cell swipe actions.
375	
376	This is the most direct explanation for the reported "appears then disappears" menu behavior.
377	
378	### H2: Long-press reorder recognizer competes with swipe recognizer
379	
380	Confidence: medium.
381	
382	Mechanism:
383	
384	- Pinned rows add a `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` for drag reorder with `minimumPressDuration = 0.35`.
385	- The recognizer has `cancelsTouchesInView = true`.
386	- Gesture delegate returns false for simultaneous recognition when either gesture is a long press.
387	- Slow/hesitant swipes could be interpreted as long press/reorder attempts, canceling the swipe action.
388	
389	Why it fits:
390	
391	- User describes inconsistent menu behavior.
392	- Pinned rows uniquely combine swipe actions and long-press reordering.
393	
394	What would prove it:
395	
396	- Simulator reproduction where slow swipes fail but fast swipes work.
397	- Gesture logs showing long-press began/canceled near failed swipe attempts.
398

41	- Impact: Dock rows load from the relay, but thread detail, Dock host filters, archive restore, archive cleanup, and local metadata can treat the same host as two different hosts.

50	## Bug North Star
51	
52	Opening a Dock row should use the relay endpoint selected from saved app config while preserving the row's stable `logicalHostID` identity. Endpoint text is transport configuration; `logicalHostID` is row identity.
53	
54	## Bug Summary
55	
56	The DockThreadCard contract intentionally split two concepts:
57	
58	- Saved phone/app config remains a host+port endpoint list.
59	- Relay cards use `logicalHostID` as stable product identity.
60	
61	The app partially honors that split. Dock row creation uses `logicalHostID`, and Dock row opening uses an alias lookup to find the configured endpoint. But thread detail then re-checks `row.id.hostID == host.id` using exact string equality. That check is still endpoint-era logic, so it rejects a valid logical-host row when the configured host id is endpoint-derived.
62	
63	Parallel read-only audits found this is not a one-file bug. The same namespace drift exists wherever a row key, filter key, metadata key, archive key, or cleanup key is compared directly to an endpoint-backed configured host id.
64

135	## Investigation
136	
137	Current failure chain:
138	
139	1. App config contains endpoint-style host entries such as `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`.
140	2. `DockHostConfiguration.id` is endpoint-derived, because it returns `endpoint.id`.
141	3. Relay `dock/subscribe` returns cards whose `logicalHostID` is `Amir-M5`.
142	4. `ThreadCardRowProjector.makeRow(card:)` sets `row.id.hostID` to `card.logicalHostID`, so the row belongs to `Amir-M5`.
143	5. `DockStore.hostConfiguration(for:)` resolves `Amir-M5` by matching `host.displayName`, so the row can be tapped.
144	6. `DockView.selectedDetailDestination` passes the resolved endpoint-backed `DockHostConfiguration` into `ThreadDetailStore`.
145	7. `ThreadDetailStore.load()` compares exact ids: `row.id.hostID == host.id`.
146	8. The exact comparison fails because `Amir-M5 != amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`, so detail renders the reported error before calling `thread/read` or `thread/resume`.
147	
148	Ranked hypotheses:
149	
150	1. Confirmed: thread detail still assumes row host id and configured host id are the same namespace. This is the direct root cause.
151	2. Supporting issue: tests use fixtures where `logicalHostID == host.id`, so they miss the endpoint-vs-logical-host split.
152	3. Unlikely: relay is emitting the wrong identity. The live payload matches the contract: cards use `logicalHostID`, and endpoint config stays separate.
153	4. Unlikely: local/home relay is down. Both relays reported healthy before this investigation, and `dock/subscribe` returned valid schema v2 card payloads.

279	## Centralization Contract
280	
281	The Swift owner is `CodexDock/State/DockHostIdentityResolver.swift`. It should
282	be a small value-type resolver plus result types, not feature-local matching
283	logic.
284	
285	- `HostRegistry` remains the endpoint-list owner.
286	- `DockHostIdentityResolver` owns every bridge between row identity and configured endpoint identity.
287	- `ThreadCardTable` owns the live Dock alias lifecycle: it stores stream host metadata from `hosts`/`upsertHosts`, records the source configured endpoint for each card, and rebuilds one resolver snapshot from configured hosts plus stream/card observations.
288	- `ThreadCardHostSnapshotLoader` must return enough host metadata and source configured endpoint context for Archive and Archive Cleanup to build the same resolver shape before projecting rows.
289	- `DockRenderInput` must carry the resolver or a resolver-built identity snapshot; projectors and views must not rebuild their own alias maps.
290	- Rows remain logical-host scoped: `DockRowViewModel.id.hostID`, `HostScopedThreadID.hostID`, and new `LocalThreadMetadataKey.hostID` values should use `DockThreadCardDTO.logicalHostID`.
291	- Saved config and network clients remain endpoint scoped: `DockHostConfiguration.id`, `DockHostConfiguration.endpoint`, WebSocket connection targets, and command clients should still use host/port endpoint config.
292	- UI filters may store endpoint ids or resolver-owned selection keys, but evaluation must call the resolver. No feature should compare `row.id.hostID` to `host.id` directly.
293	- Action callers should pass a `ResolvedDockHost` or equivalent resolver result when they need both logical row identity and endpoint transport identity. 340	The local metadata migration is part of the same fix. Without it, users can lose or duplicate labels, rails, and pins after the identity split.

343	- `ArchiveDataEngine` and `ArchiveCleanupDataEngine` must stop calling `metadataStore.load()` directly unless that call goes through the shared migration owner.
344	- The migration owner loads existing `LocalThreadMetadataKey` values, runs deterministic key normalization with a resolver, persists only when values change, and returns migrated values to every caller.
345	- No metadata store version envelope is required if the migration is proven idempotent. If a version envelope is added, this plan must update `LocalThreadMetadataStore` tests and file compatibility expectations.

347	  - Dock path: load raw metadata, synchronize streams, build resolver from configured hosts plus stream/card observations, run migration, update `DockDataEngine` local metadata, then publish the first loaded snapshot for hosts that returned rows.
348	  - Archive path: load host snapshots, build resolver from configured hosts plus archive stream/card observations, run migration, then project archive sections.

354	  - merge non-conflicting label, rail, pin state, pinned order, and last-known display fields;
355	  - never drop a pinned row silently.
356	- If a key maps to no host, leave it unchanged.
357	- If a key maps to multiple hosts, leave it unchanged and record a non-secret diagnostic.
358	- After migration, live row lookup and cached pinned de-duplication must use logical keys only.

357	            id: hostViewModel.id,
358	            displayName: hostViewModel.displayName,
359	            endpoint: hostViewModel.endpoint,
360	            observations: [:],
361	            routeDiagnostics: [:],
362	            lifecyclePhase: nil
363	        )
364	        record.routeDiagnostics[diagnostic.route] = diagnostic
365	        records[host.id] = record
366	        if !hostOrder.contains(host.id) {
367	            hostOrder.append(host.id)

372	    public func refreshRelayDiagnostics(
373	        client: RelayDiagnosticsClient = RelayDiagnosticsClient(),
374	        store: ClientObservabilityStore = .shared
375	    ) async {
376	        for host in hostConfigurations.values {
377	            do {
378	                let routes = try await client.fetchRoutes(for: host.endpoint)
379	                await store.attachRelayDiagnostics(configuredHostID: host.id, relayRoutes: routes)
380	                for route in routes {
381	                    reportRouteDiagnostic(host: host, diagnostic: route)
382	                }
383	            } catch {
384	                let diagnostic = RouteDiagnosticSnapshot(
385	                    configuredHostID: host.id,
386	                    route: "routesz",
387	                    routeStatus: .failed,
388	                    statusReasons: [
389	                        RouteStatusReason(
390	                            code: "failed:diagnostics-fetch",
391	                            message: error.localizedDescription,
392	                            actual: ObservabilityFailureCategory.downstream.rawValue,
393	                            evidenceIDs: []
394	                        )
395	                    ],
396	                    lastAttemptAt: now(),
397	                    lastFailureAt: now(),
398	                    appCritical: false,
399	                    appImpact: "diagnostic-fetch"
400	                )
401	                reportRouteDiagnostic(host: host, diagnostic: diagnostic)
402	            }
403	        }
404	    }

406	    public func reportLifecycle(_ snapshot: AppLifecycleSnapshot) {
407	        switch snapshot.phase {
408	        case .backgrounded:
409	            markAllHosts(.backgrounded("Backgrounded"))
410	        case .foregroundResuming:
411	            markAllHosts(.resuming("Resuming"))
412	        case .active:
413	            clearLifecyclePhase()
414	        case .inactive:
415	            return
416	        }
417	    }

419	    private func record(hostStates: [DockHostStateViewModel], source: ObservationSource) {
420	        for hostState in hostStates {
421	            let phase: HostConnectivityPhase
422	            switch hostState.status {
423	            case .checking:
424	                phase = .checking
425	            case .loaded(let rowCount, _):
426	                phase = .online("\(rowCount) sessions")
427	            case .degraded(_, let message):
428	                phase = .partial(message)
429	            case .empty:
430	                phase = .online("Online, no sessions")
431	            case .offline(let message):
432	                phase = .offline(message)
433	            case .error(let message):
434	                phase = .error(message)
435	            }
436	            record(host: hostState.host, source: source, phase: phase)
437	        }
438	    }

440	    private func markAllHosts(_ phase: HostConnectivityPhase) {
441	        guard !records.isEmpty else {
442	            overallStatus = rollup([])
443	            return
444	        }
445	        for id in Array(records.keys) {
446	            records[id]?.lifecyclePhase = phase
447	        }
448	        publish()
449	    }

451	    private func clearLifecyclePhase() {
452	        guard !records.isEmpty else {
453	            publishBootstrapStatusIfNeeded()
454	            return
455	        }
456	        for id in Array(records.keys) {
457	            records[id]?.lifecyclePhase = nil
458	        }
459	        publish()
460	    }

462	    private func record(
463	        host: DockHostViewModel,
464	        source: ObservationSource,
465	        phase: HostConnectivityPhase,
466	        checked: Bool = true,
467	        checkedAt: Date? = nil,
468	        successAt: Date? = nil
469	    ) {
470	        bootstrapStatus = nil
471	        let timestamp = checkedAt ?? (checked ? now() : nil)
472	        var record = records[host.id] ?? HostRecord(
473	            id: host.id,
474	            displayName: host.displayName,
475	            endpoint: host.endpoint,
476	            observations: [:],
477	            routeDiagnostics: [:],
478	            lifecyclePhase: nil
479	        )
480	        if !hostOrder.contains(host.id) {
481	            hostOrder.append(host.id)
482	        }
483	        let existingObservation = record.observations[source]
484	        let lastSuccessAt: Date?
485	        if let successAt {
486	            lastSuccessAt = successAt
487	        } else if phase.isOnlineLike {
488	            lastSuccessAt = timestamp ?? now()
489	        } else {
490	            lastSuccessAt = existingObservation?.lastSuccessAt
491	        }
492	
493	        record.observations[source] = Observation(
494	            phase: phase,
495	            lastCheckedAt: timestamp ?? existingObservation?.lastCheckedAt,
496	            lastSuccessAt: lastSuccessAt
497	        )
498	        records[host.id] = record
499	        publish()
500	    }

502	    private func publishBootstrapStatusIfNeeded() {
503	        guard records.isEmpty else {
504	            publish()
505	            return
506	        }
507	        hosts = []
508	        overallStatus = bootstrapStatus ?? .unconfigured("No relay host configured.")
509	        logOverallStatusIfNeeded(overallStatus)
510	    }
511	
512	    private func publish() {
513	        let nextHosts = records.values
514	            .map(snapshot(from:))
515	            .sorted { lhs, rhs in
516	                let leftIndex = hostIndex(lhs.id)
517	                let rightIndex = hostIndex(rhs.id)
518	                if leftIndex == rightIndex {
519	                    return lhs.displayName < rhs.displayName
520	                }
521	                return leftIndex < rightIndex
522	            }
523	        let nextOverallStatus = rollup(nextHosts)
524	        hosts = nextHosts
525	        overallStatus = nextOverallStatus
526	        logHostPhasesIfNeeded(nextHosts)
527	        logOverallStatusIfNeeded(nextOverallStatus)
528	    }

530	    private func snapshot(from record: HostRecord) -> HostConnectivitySnapshot {
531	        let observations = Array(record.observations.values)
532	        let routeDiagnostics = record.routeDiagnostics.values.sorted { $0.route < $1.route }
533	        let routePhase = phaseForRouteDiagnostics(routeDiagnostics)
534	        let observationPhase = rollupObservations(observations)
535	        return HostConnectivitySnapshot(
536	            id: record.id,
537	            displayName: record.displayName,
538	            endpoint: record.endpoint,
539	            phase: record.lifecyclePhase ?? routePhase ?? observationPhase,
540	            lastCheckedAt: latestDate(observations.compactMap(\.lastCheckedAt)),
541	            lastSuccessAt: latestDate(observations.compactMap(\.lastSuccessAt)),
542	            routeDiagnostics: routeDiagnostics
543	        )
544	    }
545	
546	    private func phaseForRouteDiagnostics(_ diagnostics: [RouteDiagnosticSnapshot]) -> HostConnectivityPhase? {
547	        guard let failed = diagnostics.first(where: { $0.appCritical && $0.routeStatus == .failed }) else {
548	            return nil
549	        }
550	        return .partial("\(failed.route) failed")
551	    }
552	
553	    private func rollupObservations(_ observations: [Observation]) -> HostConnectivityPhase {
554	        guard let strongest = observations.min(by: {
555	            priority(for: $0.phase) < priority(for: $1.phase)
556	        }) else {
557	            return .unknown
558	        }
559	        return strongest.phase
560	    }
561	
562	    private func rollup(_ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot]) -> AppConnectivityOverallStatus {
563	        guard !hosts.isEmpty else {
564	            return bootstrapStatus ?? .unconfigured("No relay host configured.")
565	        }
566	
567	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
568	            if case .configurationError = $0.phase { return true }
569	            return false
570	        }) {
571	            return .configurationError(status.phase.message)
572	        }
573	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
574	            if case .backgrounded = $0.phase { return true }
575	            return false
576	        }) {
577	            return .backgrounded("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
578	        }
579	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
580	            if case .resuming = $0.phase { return true }
581	            return false
582	        }) {
583	            return .resuming("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
584	        }
585	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
586	            if case .reconnecting = $0.phase { return true }
587	            return false
588	        }) {
589	            return .reconnecting("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
590	        }
591	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
592	            if case .stale = $0.phase { return true }
593	            return false
594	        }) {
595	            return .stale("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
596	        }
597	        let onlineLikeCount = hosts.filter { $0.phase.isOnlineLike }.count
598	        let checkingCount = hosts.filter { status in
599	            if case .checking = status.phase {
600	                return true
601	            }
602	            return false
603	        }.count
604	        if checkingCount == hosts.count {
605	            return .checking(hosts.count == 1 ? hosts[0].phase.message : "Checking \(hosts.count) hosts")
606	        }
607	        if onlineLikeCount > 0, checkingCount > 0 {
608	            return .partial("Online \(onlineLikeCount)/\(hosts.count), checking \(checkingCount)")
609	        }
610	        if onlineLikeCount == hosts.count {
611	            if let partial = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
612	                if case .partial = $0.phase { return true }
613	                return false
614	            }) {
615	                return .partial("\(partial.displayName): \(partial.phase.message)")
616	            }
617	            return .online(hosts.count == 1 ? hosts[0].phase.message : "\(hosts.count) hosts online")
618	        }
619	        if onlineLikeCount > 0 {
620	            let failing = hosts.first { !$0.phase.isOnlineLike } ?? hosts[0]
621	            return .partial("\(failing.displayName): \(failing.phase.message)")
622	        }
623	
624	        if let error = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
625	            if case .error = $0.phase { return true }
626	            return false
627	        }) {
628	            return .error("\(error.displayName): \(error.phase.message)")
629	        }
630	        if let offline = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
631	            if case .offline = $0.phase { return true }
632	            return false
633	        }) {
634	            return .offline("\(offline.displayName): \(offline.phase.message)")
635	        }
636	
637	        return .checking("Waiting for first check")
638	    }
639	
640	    private func priority(for phase: HostConnectivityPhase) -> Int {
641	        switch phase {
642	        case .configurationError:
643	            return 0
644	        case .backgrounded:
645	            return 1
646	        case .resuming:
647	            return 2
648	        case .reconnecting:
649	            return 3
650	        case .stale:
651	            return 4
652	        case .checking:
653	            return 5
654	        case .offline:
655	            return 6
656	        case .error:
657	            return 7
658	        case .partial:
659	            return 8
660	        case .online:
661	            return 9
662	        case .unknown:
663	            return 10
664	        }
665	    }
666	
667	    private func firstStatus(
668	        _ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot],
669	        matching predicate: (HostConnectivitySnapshot) -> Bool
670	    ) -> HostConnectivitySnapshot? {
671	        hosts.first(where: predicate)
672	    }
673	
674	    private func latestDate(_ dates: [Date]) -> Date? {
675	        dates.max()
676	    }
677	
678	    private func hostIndex(_ hostID: String) -> Int {
679	        hostOrder.firstIndex(of: hostID) ?? Int.max
680	    }
681	
682	    private func logHostPhasesIfNeeded(_ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot]) {
683	        for host in hosts {
684	            guard lastLoggedHostPhases[host.id] != host.phase else {
685	                continue
686	            }
687	            lastLoggedHostPhases[host.id] = host.phase
688	            DockLog.connectivity.info("connectivity host phase host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) endpoint=\(host.endpoint, privacy: .public) phase=\(host.phase.logDescription, privacy: .public) message=\(DockLog.redacted(host.phase.message), privacy: .public)")
689	        }
690	    }
691	
692	    private func logOverallStatusIfNeeded(_ status: AppConnectivityOverallStatus) {
693	        guard lastLoggedOverallStatus != status else {
694	            return
695	        }
696	        lastLoggedOverallStatus = status
697	        DockLog.connectivity.notice("connectivity overall status=\(status.label, privacy: .public) message=\(DockLog.redacted(status.message), privacy: .public)")
698	    }
699	}
700	
701	private extension HostConnectivityPhase {
702	    var logDescription: String {
703	        switch self {
704	        case .unknown:
705	            return "unknown"
706	        case .checking:
707	            return "checking"
708	        case .online:
709	            return "online"
710	        case .partial:
711	            return "partial"
712	        case .reconnecting:
713	            return "reconnecting"
714	        case .backgrounded:
715	            return "backgrounded"
716	        case .resuming:
717	            return "resuming"
718	        case .stale:
719	            return "stale"
720	        case .offline:
721	            return "offline"
722	        case .error:
723	            return "error"
724	        case .configurationError:
725	            return "configurationError"
726	        }
727	    }
728	}

124	                ?? LogicalRecord(

127	                    hasObservedLogicalIdentity: false
128	                )

131	            logicalRecordsByID[logicalHostID] = logicalRecord
132	        }

134	        var logicalIDsByAlias: [String: Set<String>] = [:]
135	        for logicalRecord in logicalRecordsByID.values {
136	            for record in logicalRecord.records {
137	                for alias in record.aliases {
138	                    logicalIDsByAlias[alias, default: []].insert(logicalRecord.logicalHostID)

182	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil,
183	        preferredConfiguredHostID: String? = nil
184	    ) -> ResolvedDockHost? {
185	        let logicalHostID = logicalHostID(
186	            forAlias: rowHostID,
187	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
188	        )
189	        guard let logicalHostID,
190	              let logicalRecord = logicalRecordsByID[logicalHostID] else {
191	            return nil
192	        }

194	        guard let selectedRecord = preferredRecord(
195	            in: logicalRecord,
196	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID,

225	            return true
226	        }

228	        if sourceLogicalIDs.isEmpty,
229	           sourceConfiguredHostID == configuredHostID {

258	        in states: [DockHostStateViewModel]
259	    ) -> DockHostStateViewModel? {
260	        guard let resolved = resolve(
261	            rowHostID: alias,
262	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
263	        ) else {
264	            return nil
265	        }
266	        return states.first { resolved.configuredHostIDs.contains($0.host.id) }
267	    }

269	    private func logicalIDs(forAlias alias: String) -> Set<String> {
270	        let trimmed = alias.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
271	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
272	            return []
273	        }
274	        return logicalIDsByAlias[trimmed]
275	            ?? logicalIDsByAlias[Self.normalizedAlias(trimmed)]
276	            ?? []
277	    }
278	
279	    private func preferredRecord(
280	        in logicalRecord: LogicalRecord,
281	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String?,
282	        preferredConfiguredHostID: String?
283	    ) -> HostRecord? {
284	        if let sourceConfiguredHostID,
285	           let record = logicalRecord.records.first(where: { $0.host.id == sourceConfiguredHostID }) {
286	            return record
287	        }
288	        if let preferredConfiguredHostID,
289	           let record = logicalRecord.records.first(where: { $0.host.id == preferredConfiguredHostID }) {
290	            return record
291	        }
292	        if let loadedRecord = logicalRecord.records.first(where: { isLoadedStatus(hostStatuses[$0.host.id]) }) {
293	            return loadedRecord
294	        }
295	        return logicalRecord.records.first
296	    }
297	
298	    private func isLoadedStatus(_ status: DockHostLoadStatus?) -> Bool {
299	        guard let status else {
300	            return false
301	        }
302	        switch status {
303	        case .loaded, .degraded, .empty:
304	            return true
305	        case .checking, .offline, .error:
306	            return false
307	        }
308	    }
309	
310	    private static func insertAlias(_ value: String?, into aliases: inout Set<String>) {
311	        guard let value = nonEmpty(value) else {
312	            return
313	        }
314	        aliases.insert(value)
315	    }
316	
317	    private static func uniqueNonEmpty(_ values: [String?]) -> [String] {
318	        var seen: Set<String> = []
319	        var result: [String] = []
320	        for value in values {
321	            guard let value = nonEmpty(value),
322	                  seen.insert(value).inserted else {
323	                continue
324	            }
325	            result.append(value)
326	        }
327	        return result
328	    }
329	
330	    private static func firstNonEmpty(_ values: [String?]) -> String? {
331	        values.lazy.compactMap(nonEmpty).first
332	    }
333	
334	    private static func nonEmpty(_ value: String?) -> String? {
335	        let trimmed = value?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
336	        guard let trimmed, !trimmed.isEmpty else {
337	            return nil
338	        }
339	        return trimmed
340	    }
341	
342	    private static func normalizedAlias(_ value: String) -> String {
343	        value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()
344	    }
345	}

38	            diagnostic.routeStatus == .failed || diagnostic.routeStatus == .blocked
39	        }) {
40	            return .failed(
41	                failed.statusReasons.first?.message ?? "\(category.title) is failing.",
42	                nextAction: "Run check or open host details."
43	            )
44	        }
45	
46	        if let degraded = diagnostics.first(where: { diagnostic in
47	            diagnostic.routeStatus == .degraded || diagnostic.routeStatus == .partial || diagnostic.routeStatus == .stale
48	        }) {
49	            return .degraded(
50	                degraded.statusReasons.first?.message ?? "\(category.title) has partial or stale evidence.",
51	                nextAction: "Run check or review technical details."
52	            )
53	        }
54	
55	        if diagnostics.contains(where: { $0.routeStatus == .healthy }) {
56	            return .healthy("\(category.title) route evidence is healthy.")
57	        }
58	
59	        return .notChecked("No completed check for \(category.title.lowercased()).")
60	    }
61	
62	    private func fallbackStatus(
63	        for category: SystemHealthCategory,
64	        overallStatus: AppConnectivityOverallStatus
65	    ) -> SystemHealthCategoryStatus {
66	        switch overallStatus {
67	        case .checking, .reconnecting, .resuming:
68	            return .checking("Checking relay health.")
69	        case .online:
70	            switch category {
71	            case .dockFeed:
72	                return .healthy("Dock feed is receiving app evidence.")
73	            case .diagnostics:
74	                return .healthy("Relay process is reachable.")
75	            case .threadDetail, .archive, .voice:
76	                return .notChecked("No recent \(category.title.lowercased()) evidence.")
77	            }
78	        case .partial:
79	            return .notChecked("No route evidence for \(category.title.lowercased()).")
80	        case .offline(let message), .error(let message), .configurationError(let message), .unconfigured(let message):
81	            return .failed(message, nextAction: "Open Relay Settings.")
82	        case .backgrounded(let message):
83	            return .stale(message, nextAction: "Bring the app foreground to refresh.")
84	        case .stale(let message):
85	            return .stale(message, nextAction: "Run check.")
86	        }
87	    }
88	
89	    private func routeNames(for category: SystemHealthCategory) -> Set<String> {
90	        switch category {
91	        case .dockFeed:
92	            return [AppServerMethods.dockSubscribe, AppServerMethods.dockUpdate, AppServerMethods.dockResync]
93	        case .threadDetail:
94	            return [
95	                AppServerMethods.threadDetailSubscribe,
96	                AppServerMethods.threadDetailUpdate,
97	                AppServerMethods.threadDetailResync,
98	            ]
99	        case .archive:
100	            return [
101	                AppServerMethods.archiveSubscribe,
102	                AppServerMethods.archiveUpdate,
103	                AppServerMethods.archiveResync,
104	                AppServerMethods.threadArchive,
105	                AppServerMethods.threadUnarchive
106	            ]
107	        case .voice:
108	            return [
109	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionStart,
110	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionAppend,
111	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionCommit,
112	                AppServerMethods.audioTranscriptionCompleted
113	            ]
114	        case .diagnostics:
115	            return [AppServerMethods.initialize, AppServerMethods.initialized]
116	        }

7	> `thread/goal/get`, app-facing `thread/loaded/list`, `/statez`, `/dbz`,

12	[CODEX_DOCK_USER_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md](CODEX_DOCK_USER_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md),
13	[CODEX_DOCK_TRUSTWORTHY_LIVE_WINDOW_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md](CODEX_DOCK_TRUSTWORTHY_LIVE_WINDOW_INTENTION_2026-06-01.md)

17	## Historical Bottom Line
18	
19	The original drift was real. Before the single-source implementation, the
20	generated Dock card contract kept the JSON payload shape aligned between relay
21	and Swift, but it did not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time,
22	row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.
23	
24	The exact pre-fix failure mode was: Dock cards were built from thread-level
25	`thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work could
26	live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. The implemented fix folds
27	those inputs through the canonical relay card projection before any Dock or
28	Archive card stream is emitted.
29	
30	Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).
31	
32	## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug
33	
34	Observed on 2026-05-31:
35	
36	- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
37	- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
38	- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
39	  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
40	  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
41	- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.
42	
43	Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.
44	
45	## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects
46	
47	The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
48	
49	Line audit:
50	
51	| File | Lines | What it protects | What it does not protect |
52	| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
53	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 6-23 | Every stream update must have `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `view`, `epoch`, and `seq`; schema version is fixed at `2`. | It does not say where `activityAtMs` must come from. |
54	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 30-95 | The stream may carry `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, `freshness`, hosts, cards, upserts, and deletes. | It does not prove a complete stream inspected turns. |
55	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 97-124 | Old session/message fields are explicitly rejected. | It only rejects obsolete fields; it does not validate semantic freshness. |
56	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 157-191 | Host-level freshness has `unknown`, `fresh`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`. | It does not define row-level freshness behavior during retained stale rows. |
57	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 223-240 | Card required fields include `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `displaySummary`, `title`, `status`, `sourceKind`, `lane`, `archiveState`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | It requires these fields to exist, not to be derived from the latest real work. |
58	| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 269-282 | `orderKey`, `activityAt`, and optional `activityAtMs` exist in the payload. | It does not say whether order uses list ordinal, thread `updatedAt`, latest turn time, or lease time. |

201	### Undocumented Contract Gaps
202	
203	These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:
204	
205	1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
206	2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
207	3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
208	4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
209	5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
210	6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
211	7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
212	8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
213	9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
214	10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
215	11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
216	12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.
