348	## Drift Inventory
349	
350	| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
351	| --- | --- | --- |
352	| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
353	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
354	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
355	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
356	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
357	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
358	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
359	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
360	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
361	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |
362	
363	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
364	
365	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
366	
367	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
368	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
369	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
370	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
371	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
372	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
373	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
374	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
375	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
376	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
377	
378	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
379	
380	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
381	
382	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
383	
384	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
385	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
386	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
387	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
388	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
389	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
390	
391	## Verdict
392	
393	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
394	
395	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

259	    private func runDockRefreshLoop() async {
260	        while !Task.isCancelled, !lifecycleCoordinator.allowsForegroundWork {
261	            do {
262	                try await Task.sleep(for: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.foregroundPollInterval)
263	            } catch {
264	                return
265	            }
266	        }
267	
268	        await dockStore.load()
269	    }

271	    private func handleScenePhase(_ scenePhase: ScenePhase) {
272	        lifecycleCoordinator.handle(appScenePhase(from: scenePhase))
273	        connectivityStore.reportLifecycle(lifecycleCoordinator.snapshot)
274	
275	        guard lifecycleCoordinator.snapshot.phase == .foregroundResuming else {
276	            return
277	        }
278	
279	        foregroundResumeTask?.cancel()
280	        foregroundResumeTask = Task {
281	            await resumeForegroundWork()
282	        }
283	    }
284	
285	    private func resumeForegroundWork() async {
286	        guard lifecycleCoordinator.snapshot.phase == .foregroundResuming else {
287	            return
288	        }
289	
290	        await dockStore.refresh()
291	        await archiveStore.refresh()
292	        lifecycleCoordinator.finishForegroundResume()
293	        connectivityStore.reportLifecycle(lifecycleCoordinator.snapshot)
294	    }

296	    private func appScenePhase(from scenePhase: ScenePhase) -> AppScenePhase {
297	        switch scenePhase {
298	        case .active:
299	            return .active
300	        case .inactive:
301	            return .inactive
302	        case .background:
303	            return .background
304	        @unknown default:
305	            return .inactive
306	        }
307	    }

250	    private func reload(showLoading: Bool) async {
251	        guard !hosts.isEmpty else {
252	            DockLog.dock.warning("dock reload skipped reason=no_hosts")
253	            return
254	        }
255	        guard !isLoading else {
256	            DockLog.dock.debug("dock reload skipped reason=already_loading")
257	            return
258	        }
259	
260	        let startedAt = Date()
261	        let signpostState = DockSignpost.dock.beginInterval("dock.reload")
262	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream reload started hosts=\(self.hosts.count, privacy: .public) show_loading=\(showLoading, privacy: .public)")
263	        isLoading = true
264	        defer {
265	            DockSignpost.dock.endInterval("dock.reload", signpostState)
266	            isLoading = false
267	        }
268	
269	        let hostViewModels = hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init)
270	        if showLoading {
271	            state = .loading(hostViewModels)
272	            screenStore.setLoading(hosts: hostViewModels)
273	            publishConnectivity(for: state)
274	        }
275	
276	        do {
277	            localMetadata = try await metadataEngine.load()
278	            DockLog.persistence.debug("dock metadata loaded entries=\(self.localMetadata.count, privacy: .public)")
279	        } catch {
280	            localMetadata = [:]
281	            await metadataEngine.replace(localMetadata)
282	            DockLog.persistence.warning("dock metadata load failed error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
283	        }
284	
285	        await dataEngine?.updateLocalMetadata(localMetadata)
286	        await dataEngine?.ensureHosts()
287	        await synchronizeStreams()
288	        await migrateMetadataHostAliases()
289	        await publishSnapshot()
290	        if case let .loaded(snapshot) = state {
291	            DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream reload finished hosts=\(self.hosts.count, privacy: .public) rows=\(snapshot.rowCount, privacy: .public) duration_ms=\(DockLog.milliseconds(since: startedAt), privacy: .public)")
292	        }
293	    }

297	    }

299	    private func publishSnapshot() async {
300	        guard !hosts.isEmpty else {
301	            return
302	        }
303	        guard let snapshot = await dataEngine?.snapshot(now: now) else {
304	            return
305	        }
306	        state = .loaded(snapshot)
307	        screenStore.publish(snapshot: snapshot)

311	    private func migrateMetadataHostAliases() async {
312	        guard let resolver = await dataEngine?.hostIdentityResolver() else {
313	            return
314	        }
315	        do {
316	            let migratedMetadata = try await metadataEngine.migrateHostAliases(using: resolver)
317	            if migratedMetadata != localMetadata {
318	                DockLog.persistence.notice("dock metadata host aliases migrated entries=\(migratedMetadata.count, privacy: .public)")
319	            }
320	            localMetadata = migratedMetadata
321	            await dataEngine?.updateLocalMetadata(localMetadata)
322	        } catch {
323	            DockLog.persistence.warning("dock metadata host alias migration failed error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
324	        }
325	    }

327	    private func publishConnectivity(for state: DockStoreState) {
328	        if connectivityEventSink == nil {
329	            connectivityReporter?.reportDockState(state)
330	        }
331	        recordConnectivityFacts(for: state)
332	    }
333	
334	    private func recordConnectivityFacts(for state: DockStoreState) {
335	        guard let connectivityEventSink else {
336	            return
337	        }
338	        let events = connectivityEvents(for: state)
339	        guard !events.isEmpty else {
340	            return
341	        }
342	        Task {
343	            for event in events {
344	                await connectivityEventSink.record(event)
345	            }
346	        }
347	    }
348	
349	    private func connectivityEvents(for state: DockStoreState) -> [ConnectivityRuntimeEvent] {
350	        switch state {
351	        case .configurationError(let message):
352	            return [
353	                ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
354	                    source: .dock,
355	                    hostID: nil,
356	                    route: "dock/configuration",
357	                    status: message,
358	                    phase: .configurationError(message),
359	                    recordedAt: now()
360	                )
361	            ]
362	        case .idle(let hosts):
363	            return hosts.map { host in
364	                ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
365	                    source: .dock,
366	                    hostID: host.id,
367	                    route: "dock",
368	                    status: "idle",
369	                    phase: .unknown,
370	                    recordedAt: now()
371	                )
372	            }
373	        case .loading(let hosts):
374	            return hosts.map { host in
375	                ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
376	                    source: .dock,
377	                    hostID: host.id,
378	                    route: "dock/subscribe",
379	                    status: "checking",
380	                    phase: .checking,
381	                    recordedAt: now()
382	                )
383	            }
384	        case .offline(let host, let message):
385	            return [
386	                ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
387	                    source: .dock,
388	                    hostID: host.id,
389	                    route: "dock/subscribe",
390	                    status: "offline: \(message)",
391	                    phase: .offline(message),
392	                    recordedAt: now()
393	                )
394	            ]
395	        case .error(let host, let message):
396	            return [
397	                ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
398	                    source: .dock,
399	                    hostID: host.id,
400	                    route: "dock/subscribe",
401	                    status: "error: \(message)",
402	                    phase: .error(message),
403	                    recordedAt: now()
404	                )
405	            ]
406	        case .loaded(let snapshot):
407	            return snapshot.hostStates.map { hostState in
408	                ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
409	                    source: .dock,
410	                    hostID: hostState.host.id,
411	                    route: "dock/subscribe",
412	                    status: hostState.status.subtitle,
413	                    phase: Self.connectivityPhase(for: hostState.status),
414	                    recordedAt: now()
415	                )
416	            }
417	        }
418	    }
419	
420	    private nonisolated static func connectivityPhase(
421	        for status: DockHostLoadStatus
422	    ) -> HostConnectivityPhase {
423	        switch status {
424	        case .checking:
425	            return .checking
426	        case .loaded(let rowCount, _):
427	            return .online("\(rowCount) sessions")
428	        case .degraded(_, let message):
429	            return .partial(message)
430	        case .empty:
431	            return .online("Online, no sessions")
432	        case .offline(let message):
433	            return .offline(message)
434	        case .error(let message):
435	            return .error(message)
436	        }
437	    }

439	    private func persistMetadataChange(
440	        logLabel: String,
441	        hostID: String?,
442	        threadID: String?,

444	    ) async {

447	            localMetadata = try await operation()
448	            await dataEngine?.updateLocalMetadata(localMetadata)
449	            setActionError(nil)
450	            await publishSnapshot()
451	            DockLog.persistence.debug("dock metadata action finished action=\(logLabel, privacy: .public) entries=\(self.localMetadata.count, privacy: .public)")
452	        } catch {
453	            DockLog.persistence.error("dock metadata action failed action=\(logLabel, privacy: .public) host_id=\(DockLog.publicID(hostID), privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(threadID), privacy: .public) error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
454	            setActionError(error.localizedDescription)
455	        }
456	    }

236	            return
237	        }
238	        didLoad = true
239	
240	        guard hostIdentityResolver.contains(
241	            rowHostID: row.hostID,
242	            sourceConfiguredHostID: row.sourceHostID,
243	            in: host.id
244	        ) else {
245	            DockLog.threadDetail.error("thread detail load failed reason=host_mismatch expected=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public) actual=\(self.row.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(self.row.threadID), privacy: .public)")
246	            let message = "This row belongs to host \(self.row.hostID), not \(self.host.id)."
247	            state = .error(
248	                header,
249	                message
250	            )
251	            screenStore.setError(header: header, message: message)
252	            return
253	        }
254	
255	        state = .loading(header)
256	        screenStore.setLoading(header)
257	        liveState = .connecting
258	        isClosing = false
259	        let startedAt = Date()
260	        DockLog.threadDetail.notice("thread detail load started host_id=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(self.row.threadID), privacy: .public)")
261	
262	        let session = factory.makeSession(for: host, foregroundWorkGate: lifecycleCoordinator)
263	        self.session = session
264	
265	        do {
266	            _ = try await session.connectAndInitialize(
267	                params: .codexDock(version: "0.1.0"),
268	                timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.connectInitializeTimeout
269	            )
270	            latestConnectionState = .connected
271	            liveEventBuffer.begin()
272	            startObservation(session: session)
273	
274	            let detailSnapshot = try await session.threadDetailSubscribe(
275	                params: ThreadDetailParams(threadId: row.threadID),
276	                timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.defaultRequestTimeout
277	            )
278	            try await replaceEvents(from: detailSnapshot, liveState: .live)
279	            await replayBufferedLiveEvents()

289	        }

520	    private func handleForegroundResuming(_ snapshot: AppLifecycleSnapshot) async {
521	        guard handledForegroundResumeGeneration != snapshot.resumeGeneration else {
522	            return
523	        }
524	        handledForegroundResumeGeneration = snapshot.resumeGeneration
525	
526	        guard !isClosing,
527	              case .loaded = state,
528	              liveState != .closed,
529	              let session else {
530	            return
531	        }
532	
533	        recoveryTask?.cancel()
534	        recoveryTask = nil
535	        if latestConnectionState == .connected {
536	            await rehydrateAfterReconnect(session: session, reason: "Resuming")
537	        } else if latestConnectionState.shouldWaitForForegroundRehydrate {
538	            markLiveSessionReconnecting("Resuming")

628	    private func queueDockRowRefresh(for marker: DockRowActivityMarker, force: Bool = false) {

630	            return

633	           pending.isNewer(than: marker) || pending == marker {
634	            return

638	        DockLog.threadDetail.notice("thread detail dock row advanced thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(self.row.threadID), privacy: .public)")

742	    private func replayBufferedLiveEvents() async {
743	        while let bufferedEvents = liveEventBuffer.takeBatch() {
744	            for event in bufferedEvents {
745	                switch event {
746	                case .notification(let notification):
747	                    await apply(notification: notification)

750	        }

754	    private func handle(notification: JSONRPCNotification) async {
755	        if liveEventBuffer.isBuffering {
756	            liveEventBuffer.append(notification: notification)
757	            DockLog.threadDetail.debug("thread notification buffered during canonical load method=\(notification.method, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(self.row.threadID), privacy: .public)")
758	            return
759	        }

763	    private func apply(notification: JSONRPCNotification) async {
764	        guard notification.method == AppServerMethods.threadDetailUpdate else {
765	            return
766	        }
767	
768	        do {
769	            let update = try notification.params?.decoded(as: ThreadDetailUpdateDTO.self)
770	            guard let update else {
771	                return

5	protocol ThreadCardStreamLifecycleDelegate: AnyObject {
6	    func cardStreamLifecycleMarkChecking(host: DockHostConfiguration) async
7	    func cardStreamLifecycleMarkFailure(_ failure: DockRequestFailure, host: DockHostConfiguration) async
8	    func cardStreamLifecycleApplySnapshot(
9	        _ update: ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO,
10	        host: DockHostConfiguration
11	    ) async -> ThreadCardTableApplyResult
12	    func cardStreamLifecycleApplyUpdate(
13	        _ update: ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO,
14	        host: DockHostConfiguration
15	    ) async -> ThreadCardTableApplyResult
16	    func cardStreamLifecycleRowCount(for host: DockHostConfiguration) async -> Int
17	    func cardStreamLifecyclePublishSnapshot() async
18	    func cardStreamLifecycleMigrateMetadataHostAliases() async
19	}
20	
21	@MainActor
22	final class ThreadCardStreamLifecycle {
23	    private let view: ThreadCardStreamView
24	    private let streamClient: any ThreadCardStreamConnecting
25	    private let streamReconnectDelay: Duration
26	    private let streamHeartbeatTimeout: Duration
27	    private let logger: Logger
28	    private let logName: String
29	    private weak var delegate: (any ThreadCardStreamLifecycleDelegate)?
30	
31	    private var streamConnections: [String: any ThreadCardStreamConnection] = [:]
32	    private var streamTasks: [String: Task<Void, Never>] = [:]
33	    private var streamHeartbeatTasks: [String: Task<Void, Never>] = [:]
34	    private var streamHeartbeatTokens: [String: UUID] = [:]
35	
36	    init(
37	        view: ThreadCardStreamView,
38	        streamClient: any ThreadCardStreamConnecting,
39	        streamReconnectDelay: Duration,
40	        streamHeartbeatTimeout: Duration,
41	        logger: Logger,
42	        logName: String,
43	        delegate: any ThreadCardStreamLifecycleDelegate
44	    ) {
45	        self.view = view
46	        self.streamClient = streamClient
47	        self.streamReconnectDelay = streamReconnectDelay
48	        self.streamHeartbeatTimeout = streamHeartbeatTimeout
49	        self.logger = logger
50	        self.logName = logName
51	        self.delegate = delegate
52	    }
53	
54	    deinit {
55	        streamTasks.values.forEach { $0.cancel() }
56	        streamHeartbeatTasks.values.forEach { $0.cancel() }
57	    }
58	
59	    func synchronizeStreams(hosts: [DockHostConfiguration]) async {
60	        let validHostIDs = Set(hosts.map(\.id))
61	        for hostID in streamConnections.keys where !validHostIDs.contains(hostID) {
62	            streamTasks[hostID]?.cancel()
63	            streamTasks[hostID] = nil
64	            streamHeartbeatTasks[hostID]?.cancel()
65	            streamHeartbeatTasks[hostID] = nil
66	            streamHeartbeatTokens[hostID] = nil
67	            let connection = streamConnections.removeValue(forKey: hostID)
68	            await connection?.close()
69	        }
70	
71	        for host in hosts {
72	            if let connection = streamConnections[host.id] {
73	                await resync(host: host, connection: connection)
74	            } else {
75	                await openStream(host: host)
76	            }
77	        }
78	    }
79	
80	    func closeStreams() async {
81	        streamTasks.values.forEach { $0.cancel() }
82	        streamTasks = [:]
83	        streamHeartbeatTasks.values.forEach { $0.cancel() }
84	        streamHeartbeatTasks = [:]
85	        streamHeartbeatTokens = [:]
86	        let connections = streamConnections
87	        streamConnections = [:]
88	        for connection in connections.values {
89	            await connection.close()
90	        }
91	    }
92	
93	    private func openStream(host: DockHostConfiguration) async {
94	        guard let delegate else {
95	            return
96	        }
97	
98	        await delegate.cardStreamLifecycleMarkChecking(host: host)
99	        await delegate.cardStreamLifecyclePublishSnapshot()
100	        var openedConnection: (any ThreadCardStreamConnection)?
101	        do {
102	            let connection = try await streamClient.connect(to: host)
103	            openedConnection = connection
104	            streamConnections[host.id] = connection
105	            let snapshot = try await connection.subscribe()
106	            try await applySubscribedSnapshot(snapshot, host: host, connection: connection)
107	            recordStreamActivity(host: host, connection: connection)
108	            startUpdateTask(host: host, connection: connection)
109	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecycleMigrateMetadataHostAliases()
110	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecyclePublishSnapshot()
111	        } catch {
112	            streamTasks[host.id]?.cancel()
113	            streamTasks[host.id] = nil
114	            streamHeartbeatTasks[host.id]?.cancel()
115	            streamHeartbeatTasks[host.id] = nil
116	            streamHeartbeatTokens[host.id] = nil
117	            streamConnections[host.id] = nil
118	            await openedConnection?.close()
119	            logger.warning("\(self.logName, privacy: .public) stream open failed view=\(self.view.rawValue, privacy: .public) host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
120	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecycleMarkFailure(Self.mapRequestFailure(error), host: host)
121	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecyclePublishSnapshot()
122	        }
123	    }
124	
125	    private func resync(host: DockHostConfiguration, connection: any ThreadCardStreamConnection) async {
126	        guard let delegate else {
127	            return
128	        }
129	
130	        do {
131	            let snapshot = try await connection.resync()
132	            try await applyResyncSnapshot(snapshot, host: host)
133	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecycleMigrateMetadataHostAliases()
134	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecyclePublishSnapshot()
135	            let rowCount = await delegate.cardStreamLifecycleRowCount(for: host)
136	            logger.notice("\(self.logName, privacy: .public) stream resync finished view=\(self.view.rawValue, privacy: .public) host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) seq=\(snapshot.seq, privacy: .public) rows=\(rowCount, privacy: .public)")
137	        } catch {
138	            logger.warning("\(self.logName, privacy: .public) stream resync failed view=\(self.view.rawValue, privacy: .public) host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
139	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecycleMarkFailure(Self.mapRequestFailure(error), host: host)
140	            await delegate.cardStreamLifecyclePublishSnapshot()
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    private func startUpdateTask(host: DockHostConfiguration, connection: any ThreadCardStreamConnection) {
145	        streamTasks[host.id]?.cancel()
146	        streamTasks[host.id] = Task { [weak self, host, connection] in
147	            do {
148	                for try await update in connection.updates() {
149	                    await self?.handleStreamUpdate(update, host: host, connection: connection)
150	                }

1	# Codex Dock Client
2	
3	This repo is the Swift client for the Codex Dock MVP.
4	
5	## App-Server Runbook
6	
7	There are two different app-server modes we need to keep separate.
8	
9	### 1. Normal daemon mode
10	
11	The Codex daemon is the normal local background service:
12	
13	```sh
14	rtk codex app-server daemon restart
15	rtk codex app-server daemon version
16	```
17	
18	Today, this daemon always starts its managed app-server on a Unix socket:
19	
20	```sh
21	app-server --remote-control --listen unix://
22	```
23	
24	That socket is:
25	
26	```text
27	/Users/aelaguiz/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock
28	```
29	
30	This is fine for local Codex tooling, but it is not reachable from an iPhone.
31	
32	### 2. Loopback WebSocket mode
33	
34	For local WebSocket development, start a direct app-server process in loopback
35	mode:
36	
37	```sh
38	rtk codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:4500
39	```
40	
41	Then the Swift test can point at:
42	
43	```sh
44	rtk env CODEX_DOCK_LOOPBACK_APP_SERVER_WS=ws://127.0.0.1:4500 swift test
45	```
46	
47	Important: loopback is only a local development step. It is not Phase 1
48	completion evidence, because an iPhone cannot use the Mac's `127.0.0.1`. The
49	phone-reachable acceptance test intentionally rejects loopback endpoints.
50	
51	After a loopback smoke run, stop the direct `codex app-server --listen
52	ws://127.0.0.1:4500` process and restart the normal daemon:
53	
54	```sh
55	rtk codex app-server daemon restart
56	```
57	
58	That restart restores the daemon's normal Unix-socket service. It does not move
59	the daemon itself into loopback WebSocket mode; current Codex daemon startup
60	does not expose that setting.
61	
62	### 3. Phone-reachable relay mode
63	
64	The raw Codex app-server still runs with bearer auth on the Mac. The iPhone does
65	not connect to that raw server directly. It connects to the Dock relay on the
66	Mac, and the relay uses the raw app-server token behind the scenes.
67	
68	```sh
69	rtk make services
70	```
71	
72	The phone-facing endpoint is:
73	
74	```text
75	<amir-m5-lan-or-tailscale-host>:4510
76	```
77	
78	For the personal LAN/Tailscale path, the relay accepts the iPhone without a
79	client bearer token. The relay advertises `_codexdock._tcp` with non-secret
80	Bonjour metadata so the app can find it after a normal home-screen launch.
81	
82	## Physical Phone Rule
83	
84	Mocks, scripted transports, Unix sockets, and loopback-only WebSockets do not
85	complete the physical phone path. The current phone path is the Dock relay on
86	`:4510`, with no iPhone-side bearer token. The iPhone 17 Pro uses
87	`ws://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` and
88	`ws://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`; the iPhone 14 uses
89	`ws://Amir-M5.local:4510` and `ws://192.168.50.74:4510`.
90	
91	Physical-device proof is Makefile-owned. Use `rtk make device-install` and
92	`rtk make device-config-verify`; if a phone is actively in use, unavailable, or
93	blocked by device tooling, record the exact skipped command and exact blocker.
94	Simulator, local relay, service-status, and generated-artifact proof only prove
95	the parts they actually exercise.
96	
97	## Exhaustive Sync Harness
98	
99	The repeatable over-time sync proof is documented in
100	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_RUNBOOK_2026-05-31.md`.
101	
102	Use it when checking whether Codex storage, app-server state, relay projection,
103	client-used routes, and the literal `iPhone 17` simulator display stay in sync.
104	The harness treats lag over the configured budget as a failure, even if a later
105	sample eventually catches up.
106	
107	## Canonical Service Start
108	
109	Use this target for local Dock development instead of manually starting and
110	stopping host services:
111	
112	```sh
113	rtk make services
114	```
115	
116	It starts/reuses two real services and leaves them running:
117	
118	- Raw Codex app-server on loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`
119	- Dock relay on `ws://<APP_SERVER_HOST>:4510`
120	
121	The raw app-server provides stored history. The relay is the app endpoint. Dock
122	Home subscribes to relay-owned `dock/*` methods: `dock/subscribe` returns the
123	first normalized snapshot, `dock/update` pushes deltas and heartbeats, and
124	`dock/resync` returns a replacement snapshot if the client detects a sequence
125	gap. The relay materializes app-server thread projections in SQLite at
126	`.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`, serves Dock Home from that state store, and
127	keeps stale rows visible when a source refresh fails.
128	
129	Card truth has one path. The relay may inspect raw app-server facts such as
130	`thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, live events, and live loaded
131	IDs internally, but Swift never uses those raw routes to prove Dock or Archive
132	cards. Swift renders card truth only from `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams.
133	
134	Row text has two separate meanings. Raw history `preview` is preserved as the
135	app-server's stored preview and may be the opening message. Dock overview rows
136	use relay-owned card fields from the canonical projection. That projection may
137	inspect newest turns and live events to compute honest activity, but any
138	unproven card makes the stream partial or stale instead of pretending the list
139	is fresh.
140	
141	The relay also owns OpenAI Realtime transcription. Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the
142	Mac environment or repo `.env`; the app never receives it. The default Realtime
143	transcription model is `gpt-realtime-whisper`, with optional Mac-side
144	`CODEX_DOCK_OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` and
145	`CODEX_DOCK_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_DELAY` overrides.
146	
147	The Dock filters loaded thread cards locally. It opens to `Newest`: one flat
148	newest-first list across configured hosts. Rows carry their own short host
149	name, repository or working directory, branch, status, last activity, local
150	label, and latest summary. `Host` and `Branch` are Dock lenses, not app-level
151	tabs or a separate sort picker; both preserve newest-first ordering inside
152	their groups. `Filters` opens one shared filter surface for host, branch,
153	canonical Dock status, repository or working directory, source, and the fixed
154	`Newest activity` sort. Status `Any` includes `Idle`, so idle rows are visible
155	by default and can be narrowed through the status filter. Search is full-width and
156	matches session title, label, repository or working directory, branch, summary,
157	status, host display name, host id, source, and thread id. Codex runtime
158	`notLoaded` is normalized by the relay to Dock `dormant`; Dock Home does not
159	spend row-badge space on that background state.
160	
161	The app has one root connectivity indicator. It appears above Dock and opens
162	the `System Health` sheet for relay and route diagnostics. Archive recovery,
163	cleanup, and relay host editing live in the Dock `More` menu as `Archived
164	Threads`, `Archive Cleanup`, and `Relay Settings` task sheets, not app-level
165	tabs. The labels are `Unconfigured`,
166	`Checking`, `Online`, `Partial`, `Reconnecting`, `Backgrounded`, `Resuming`,
167	`Stale`, `Offline`, `Error`, and `Config error`. A nil host bearer token is
168	normal for the personal physical-phone relay path; it is not shown as missing
169	credentials.
170	
171	Live Session detail connections reconnect automatically when recovery is safe.
172	Swift consumes relay-owned `thread/detail/subscribe`, `thread/detail/update`,
173	and `thread/detail/resync` projection rows. The relay may still use raw
174	`thread/read includeTurns:false`, paged `thread/turns/list`, and upstream
175	`thread/resume excludeTurns:true` internally, but those raw routes are not the
176	phone-facing Thread Detail display contract. Failed user sends are not silently
177	replayed. If the relay loses its upstream session, it either re-resumes upstream
178	or closes the phone WebSocket so Swift can mark the detail stale or reconnect.
179	
180	When iOS backgrounds the app, root refresh and reconnect attempts pause instead
181	of spending retry budget. Open details keep visible events, request action
182	state, and draft text but are no longer labeled fresh. Active voice capture is
183	cancelled without auto-submitting. On foreground resume, Dock and Archive
184	refresh from root, open details rehydrate through `thread/detail/resync`, and
185	the indicator moves through `Backgrounded` / `Resuming` / `Reconnecting` as
186	appropriate.
187	
188	The service targets install per-repo launchd files on macOS and systemd user
189	files on Linux, with runtime files under `.codex-dock/`:

191	```text
192	.codex-dock/services/com.aelaguiz.codex-dock.app-server.plist

205	The default app endpoint is:

209	```

218	Process health, route health, and card freshness are separate. `/readyz` only
219	means the relay process can answer HTTP. `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`,

251	services.

253	## Cross-Platform Host Services

# Codex Dock Client

This repo is the Swift client for the Codex Dock MVP.

## App-Server Runbook

There are two different app-server modes we need to keep separate.

### 1. Normal daemon mode

The Codex daemon is the normal local background service:

```sh
rtk codex app-server daemon restart
rtk codex app-server daemon version
```

Today, this daemon always starts its managed app-server on a Unix socket:

```sh
app-server --remote-control --listen unix://
```

That socket is:

```text
/Users/aelaguiz/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock
```

This is fine for local Codex tooling, but it is not reachable from an iPhone.

### 2. Loopback WebSocket mode

For local WebSocket development, start a direct app-server process in loopback
mode:

```sh
rtk codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:4500
```

Then the Swift test can point at:

```sh
rtk env CODEX_DOCK_LOOPBACK_APP_SERVER_WS=ws://127.0.0.1:4500 swift test
```

Important: loopback is only a local development step. It is not Phase 1
completion evidence, because an iPhone cannot use the Mac's `127.0.0.1`. The
phone-reachable acceptance test intentionally rejects loopback endpoints.

After a loopback smoke run, stop the direct `codex app-server --listen
ws://127.0.0.1:4500` process and restart the normal daemon:

```sh
rtk codex app-server daemon restart
```

That restart restores the daemon's normal Unix-socket service. It does not move
the daemon itself into loopback WebSocket mode; current Codex daemon startup
does not expose that setting.

### 3. Phone-reachable relay mode

The raw Codex app-server still runs with bearer auth on the Mac. The iPhone does
not connect to that raw server directly. It connects to the Dock relay on the
Mac, and the relay uses the raw app-server token behind the scenes.

```sh
rtk make services
```

The phone-facing endpoint is:

```text
<amir-m5-lan-or-tailscale-host>:4510
```

For the personal LAN/Tailscale path, the relay accepts the iPhone without a
client bearer token. The relay advertises `_codexdock._tcp` with non-secret
Bonjour metadata so the app can find it after a normal home-screen launch.

## Physical Phone Rule

Mocks, scripted transports, Unix sockets, and loopback-only WebSockets do not
complete the physical phone path. The current phone path is the Dock relay on
`:4510`, with no iPhone-side bearer token. The iPhone 17 Pro uses
`ws://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` and
`ws://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`; the iPhone 14 uses
`ws://Amir-M5.local:4510` and `ws://192.168.50.74:4510`.

Physical-device proof is Makefile-owned. Use `rtk make device-install` and
`rtk make device-config-verify`; if a phone is actively in use, unavailable, or
blocked by device tooling, record the exact skipped command and exact blocker.
Simulator, local relay, service-status, and generated-artifact proof only prove
the parts they actually exercise.

## Exhaustive Sync Harness

The repeatable over-time sync proof is documented in
`docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_RUNBOOK_2026-05-31.md`.

Use it when checking whether Codex storage, app-server state, relay projection,
client-used routes, and the literal `iPhone 17` simulator display stay in sync.
The harness treats lag over the configured budget as a failure, even if a later
sample eventually catches up.

## Canonical Service Start

Use this target for local Dock development instead of manually starting and
stopping host services:

```sh
rtk make services
```

It starts/reuses two real services and leaves them running:

- Raw Codex app-server on loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`
- Dock relay on `ws://<APP_SERVER_HOST>:4510`

The raw app-server provides stored history. The relay is the app endpoint. Dock
Home subscribes to relay-owned `dock/*` methods: `dock/subscribe` returns the
first normalized snapshot, `dock/update` pushes deltas and heartbeats, and
`dock/resync` returns a replacement snapshot if the client detects a sequence
gap. The relay materializes app-server thread projections in SQLite at
`.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`, serves Dock Home from that state store, and
keeps stale rows visible when a source refresh fails.

Card truth has one path. The relay may inspect raw app-server facts such as
`thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, live events, and live loaded
IDs internally, but Swift never uses those raw routes to prove Dock or Archive
cards. Swift renders card truth only from `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams.

Row text has two separate meanings. Raw history `preview` is preserved as the
app-server's stored preview and may be the opening message. Dock overview rows
use relay-owned card fields from the canonical projection. That projection may
inspect newest turns and live events to compute honest activity, but any
unproven card makes the stream partial or stale instead of pretending the list
is fresh.

The relay also owns OpenAI Realtime transcription. Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the
Mac environment or repo `.env`; the app never receives it. The default Realtime
transcription model is `gpt-realtime-whisper`, with optional Mac-side
`CODEX_DOCK_OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` and
`CODEX_DOCK_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_DELAY` overrides.

The Dock filters loaded thread cards locally. It opens to `Newest`: one flat
newest-first list across configured hosts. Rows carry their own short host
name, repository or working directory, branch, status, last activity, local
label, and latest summary. `Host` and `Branch` are Dock lenses, not app-level
tabs or a separate sort picker; both preserve newest-first ordering inside
their groups. `Filters` opens one shared filter surface for host, branch,
canonical Dock status, repository or working directory, source, and the fixed
`Newest activity` sort. Status `Any` includes `Idle`, so idle rows are visible
by default and can be narrowed through the status filter. Search is full-width and
matches session title, label, repository or working directory, branch, summary,
status, host display name, host id, source, and thread id. Codex runtime
`notLoaded` is normalized by the relay to Dock `dormant`; Dock Home does not
spend row-badge space on that background state.

The app has one root connectivity indicator. It appears above Dock and opens
the `System Health` sheet for relay and route diagnostics. Archive recovery,
cleanup, and relay host editing live in the Dock `More` menu as `Archived
Threads`, `Archive Cleanup`, and `Relay Settings` task sheets, not app-level
tabs. The labels are `Unconfigured`,
`Checking`, `Online`, `Partial`, `Reconnecting`, `Backgrounded`, `Resuming`,
`Stale`, `Offline`, `Error`, and `Config error`. A nil host bearer token is
normal for the personal physical-phone relay path; it is not shown as missing
credentials.

Live Session detail connections reconnect automatically when recovery is safe.
Swift consumes relay-owned `thread/detail/subscribe`, `thread/detail/update`,
and `thread/detail/resync` projection rows. The relay may still use raw
`thread/read includeTurns:false`, paged `thread/turns/list`, and upstream
`thread/resume excludeTurns:true` internally, but those raw routes are not the
phone-facing Thread Detail display contract. Failed user sends are not silently
replayed. If the relay loses its upstream session, it either re-resumes upstream
or closes the phone WebSocket so Swift can mark the detail stale or reconnect.

When iOS backgrounds the app, root refresh and reconnect attempts pause instead
of spending retry budget. Open details keep visible events, request action
state, and draft text but are no longer labeled fresh. Active voice capture is
cancelled without auto-submitting. On foreground resume, Dock and Archive
refresh from root, open details rehydrate through `thread/detail/resync`, and
the indicator moves through `Backgrounded` / `Resuming` / `Reconnecting` as

and `/syncz` expose process and route health only; they do not prove Dock or

```sh

app-server-status`, or `rtk make dock-relay-status`; it should not stop the
services.

## Diagnostics Commands

The iOS app writes Apple unified logs under subsystem
`com.aelaguiz.CodexDock`. The Dock relay writes structured JSON lines to
stderr, which the service target stores at
`.codex-dock/logs/dock-relay.err.log`.

The app also writes app-owned route evidence under
`Library/Application Support/CodexDock/Diagnostics/`. This is the preferred
physical-device artifact path when Apple unified log collection is blocked.

Fetch a relay debug bundle:

```sh
rtk make relay-debug-bundle
```

Compare configured relay hosts:

```sh
rtk make relay-host-compare HOSTS=amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510,home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510
```

Copy app-owned diagnostics from a simulator:

```sh
rtk make sim-debug-bundle SIM='iPhone 14'
```

Copy app-owned diagnostics from a physical iPhone:

```sh
rtk make device-debug-bundle DEVICE=<device-udid>
```

Stream simulator logs:

```sh
rtk make sim-logs SIM='iPhone 17'
```

Collect physical device logs:

```sh
rtk make device-logs DEVICE=<device-udid>
```

On some Xcode installs, physical log collection requires root. If this prints
`log: Must be root to collect logs from attached device`, rerun the raw
`xcrun log collect` command with root privileges or treat that as the log
collection blocker.

```sh
rtk make dock-relay-logs
```

## Simulator Commands

Start the simulator app path for a specific simulator:

```sh
rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
```

Or use a simulator ID:

```sh
rtk make app SIM=DEF1631B-7125-43C6-BFA3-4423BF103C91
```

That command starts/reuses the persistent services and boots the simulator in
the background. If `com.aelaguiz.CodexDockApp` is already running on that
simulator, it leaves the app alone and skips build/install/launch so Simulator
does not keep stealing focus.

Force a replacement build and launch only when you actually need it:

```sh
FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM=DEF1631B-7125-43C6-BFA3-4423BF103C91
```

When it does launch, it uses generated app config from `.codex-dock/host.env`.
It does not pass an OpenAI key or app-server bearer token into the app.

Run the generated-project app tests through the same Makefile-owned path:

```sh
rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'
```

Verify the generated app-safe relay config used by simulator launches:

```sh
rtk make sim-config-verify SIM='iPhone 17'
```

When these targets build, they stamp debug builds with `APP_BUILD_NUMBER` so
stale simulator artifacts fail verification instead of silently launching.

Start all local services the app currently needs:

```sh
rtk make services
```

Today that means the authenticated raw loopback app-server plus the
no-client-auth Dock relay. If another local service becomes required later, add
it behind this target so `rtk make app SIM=...` keeps doing the whole setup
idempotently.

The service targets write host-side settings to `.codex-dock/service.env`,
write app-safe settings to `.codex-dock/host.env`, and leave the user-owned
`.env` untouched. They may read `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the shell or `.env`, but
they must not rewrite `.env`.

`.codex-dock/service.env` may contain host-side secrets and relay provider
settings:

```text
CODEX_DOCK_HOSTS=amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510
CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_ID=Amir-M5
CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_NAME=Amir-M5
CODEX_DOCK_OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL=gpt-realtime-whisper
CODEX_DOCK_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_DELAY=low
OPENAI_API_KEY=<kept on Mac when configured>
```

`.codex-dock/host.env` is the generated app config. It must stay non-secret:

```text
CODEX_DOCK_HOSTS=amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510
```

List available simulators:

```sh
rtk make sims
```

Boot and open one simulator explicitly:

```sh
rtk make sim SIM='iPhone 17'
```

If a name matches more than one simulator, use the ID from `rtk make sims`:

```sh
rtk make sim SIM=DEF1631B-7125-43C6-BFA3-4423BF103C91
```

This writes accessibility-state proof to `/tmp/codex-client/.../sim-ui-dump.json`
and `/tmp/codex-client/.../sim-ui-dump.md`. The JSON contains the visible
screen, visible Dock rows or Thread Detail messages when present, rollups, and
the raw accessibility element list. If the app is not running or the current
screen cannot be classified, the target writes a blocked/non-fresh report
instead of silently passing.

behavior is fixed:

```sh

```

The matrix mutates controlled Codex data, watches relay truth, samples the
literal simulator accessibility state over time, and fails when the UI does not
converge within the configured lag budget. It also checks visible Dock row
order and Thread Detail message order from top-to-bottom accessibility frames
in the scenarios where ordering matters. The proof reports are schema-checked
by `rtk npm run contract:check`.

The generated-project test target includes UI automation smoke tests. Those
tests use the accessibility tree as the primary proof: screens, controls, rows,
visible state banners, and visible error states expose stable
`codexdock.*` automation identifiers plus accessibility values where the state
matters. Screenshots are useful triage evidence, but they are not the selector
strategy for this workflow.

two-host relay list: `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` and

```sh

```

Builds and installs are Makefile-owned. Do not use raw Xcode, CoreDevice,
simulator install, or Flutter build/install commands as the normal workflow;
add or fix a make target instead. Raw platform commands are for diagnosing a
failed make target.

Do not use fixture or SwiftUI preview rows as production evidence. A physical
phone pass means the installed app connects to the real relay-backed host path,
renders real `DockThreadCard` rows, and shows offline/error UI when that same
host path is unavailable. While physical testing is deferred, the agent-side
stand-in is simulator plus local/real-relay/service-status proof, with the
physical checks recorded for Amir.

3	struct ThreadCardRowProjector {
4	    let hosts: [DockHostConfiguration]
5	    let hostIdentityResolver: DockHostIdentityResolver
6	    let localMetadata: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
7	    let now: @Sendable () -> Date
8	
9	    func rows(from cards: [DockThreadCardDTO]) -> [DockRowViewModel] {
10	        cards.filter(\.isAppFacingHumanThreadCard).map { card in
11	            makeRow(card: card)
12	        }
13	    }
14	
15	    func makeRow(card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> DockRowViewModel {
16	        guard let resolvedSourceHostID = nonEmpty(card.sourceHostID),
17	              let projectionID = nonEmpty(card.projectionID),
18	              let displayOrderKey = nonEmpty(card.displayOrderKey) else {
19	            preconditionFailure("ThreadCardRowProjector only accepts relay projection rows with sourceHostID, projectionID, and displayOrderKey")
20	        }
21	        // Dock rows are projection rows. `logicalHostID` is display payload only;
22	        // action identity follows the relay-owned source host namespace.
23	        let id = HostScopedThreadID(hostID: resolvedSourceHostID, threadID: card.threadID)
24	        let metadata = metadata(
25	            for: id,
26	            backendSessionID: card.backendSessionID,
27	            sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID
28	        )
29	        let activityDate = activityDate(for: card)
30	        return DockRowViewModel(
31	            threadIdentity: id,
32	            sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID,
33	            projectionID: projectionID,
34	            backendSessionID: card.backendSessionID,
35	            title: nonEmpty(card.title) ?? "Thread \(shortThreadID(card.threadID))",
36	            hostDisplayName: nonEmpty(card.hostDisplayName)
37	                ?? hostDisplayName(for: card.logicalHostID, sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID),
38	            hostEndpoint: nonEmpty(card.hostEndpoint)
39	                ?? hostEndpoint(for: card.logicalHostID, sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID),
40	            repository: nonEmpty(card.repository) ?? nonEmpty(card.workingDirectory) ?? "Unknown workspace",
41	            branch: nonEmpty(card.branch) ?? "No branch",
42	            status: status(for: card.status),
43	            lastActivity: relativeTime(since: activityDate),
44	            lastActivityDate: activityDate,
45	            displayOrderKey: displayOrderKey,
46	            summary: nonEmpty(card.displaySummary) ?? "No summary",
47	            rail: metadata?.rail ?? rail(for: card),
48	            label: metadata?.label,
49	            origin: origin(for: card),
50	            relationship: relationship(for: card),
51	            isPinned: metadata?.isPinned ?? false,
52	            pinnedAt: metadata?.pinnedAt,
53	            pinnedOrder: metadata?.pinnedOrder
54	        )
55	    }
56	
57	    private func metadata(
58	        for id: HostScopedThreadID,
59	        backendSessionID: String,
60	        sourceHostID: String?
61	    ) -> LocalThreadMetadata? {
62	        let exactKey = LocalThreadMetadataKey(
63	            hostID: id.hostID,
64	            backendSessionID: backendSessionID,
65	            threadID: id.threadID
66	        )
67	        if let metadata = localMetadata[exactKey] {
68	            return metadata
69	        }
70	
71	        return localMetadata.first { key, _ in
72	            guard key.backendSessionID == backendSessionID,
73	                  key.threadID == id.threadID else {
74	                return false
75	            }
76	            return hostIdentityResolver.logicalHostID(
77	                forAlias: key.hostID,
78	                sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID
79	            ) == id.hostID
80	        }?.value
81	    }
82	
83	    private func activityDate(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> Date {
84	        // The relay owns card recency. If this timestamp is missing, decoding
85	        // fails at the DTO boundary instead of letting Swift invent an order.
86	        Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(card.activityAtMs) / 1_000)
87	    }
88	
89	    private func status(for status: DockThreadCardStatus) -> DockRowStatusKind {
90	        switch status {
91	        case .running:
92	            return .running
93	        case .needsInput:
94	            return .needsInput
95	        case .needsApproval:
96	            return .needsApproval
97	        case .idle:
98	            return .idle
99	        case .error:
100	            return .error
101	        case .dormant:
102	            return .dormant
103	        case .unknown:
104	            return .unknown
105	        }
106	    }
107	
108	    private func origin(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> SessionOrigin {
109	        switch card.lane {
110	        case .human:
111	            return .humanInteractive(subtype: .cli)
112	        case .agent:
113	            return .agentOrAutomation(subtype: .exec)
114	        case .unknown:
115	            switch card.sourceKind {
116	            case .human:
117	                return .humanInteractive(subtype: .cli)
118	            case .automation:
119	                return .agentOrAutomation(subtype: .exec)
120	            case .unknown:
121	                return .unknown()
122	            }
123	        }
124	    }
125	
126	    private func relativeTime(since date: Date) -> String {
127	        guard date != .distantPast else {
128	            return "No activity"
129	        }
130	        let seconds = max(0, Int(now().timeIntervalSince(date)))
131	
132	        switch seconds {
133	        case 0..<60:
134	            return "now"
135	        case 60..<3_600:
136	            return "\(seconds / 60)m ago"
137	        case 3_600..<86_400:
138	            return "\(seconds / 3_600)h ago"
139	        default:
140	            return "\(seconds / 86_400)d ago"
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    private func relationship(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> DockRowThreadRelationship {
145	        switch card.relationship {
146	        case .forked:
147	            return .forked
148	        case .root, .spawned:
149	            return .root
150	        case .unknown, nil:
151	            return .root
152	        }
153	    }
154	
155	    private func rail(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> DockRowRail {
156	        let rails = DockRowRail.allCases
157	        let checksum = card.threadID.utf8.reduce(UInt64(0)) { partial, byte in
158	            (partial &* 31) &+ UInt64(byte)
159	        }
160	        return rails[Int(checksum % UInt64(rails.count))]
161	    }
162	
163	    private func nonEmpty(_ value: String?) -> String? {
164	        let trimmed = value?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
165	        if let trimmed, !trimmed.isEmpty {
166	            return trimmed
167	        }
168	        return nil
169	    }
170	
171	    private func hostDisplayName(for hostID: String, sourceHostID: String? = nil) -> String {
172	        hostIdentityResolver.displayName(forAlias: hostID, sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID)
173	            ?? hostID
174	    }
175	
176	    private func hostEndpoint(for hostID: String, sourceHostID: String? = nil) -> String {
177	        hostIdentityResolver.endpoint(forAlias: hostID, sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID)
178	            ?? hostID
179	    }
180	
181	    private func shortThreadID(_ threadID: String) -> String {
182	        if threadID.count <= 12 {
183	            return threadID
184	        }
185	        return String(threadID.prefix(8))
186	    }
187	}

90	    func save(
91	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
92	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
93	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]

99	public actor FileLocalThreadMetadataStore: LocalThreadMetadataStoring {
100	    private struct Entry: Codable {
101	        let key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
102	        let metadata: LocalThreadMetadata
103	    }
104	
105	    private let fileURL: URL
106	    private var cache: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]?
107	
108	    public init(fileURL: URL = FileLocalThreadMetadataStore.defaultFileURL()) {
109	        self.fileURL = fileURL
110	    }
111	
112	    public func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
113	        if let cache {
114	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load cache hit entries=\(cache.count, privacy: .public)")
115	            return cache
116	        }
117	
118	        let loaded: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
119	        if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) {
120	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load started path=\(self.fileURL.path, privacy: .public)")
121	            let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)
122	            let entries = try JSONDecoder().decode([Entry].self, from: data)
123	            loaded = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: entries.map { ($0.key, $0.metadata) })
124	        } else {
125	            loaded = [:]
126	        }
127	        cache = loaded
128	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load finished entries=\(loaded.count, privacy: .public)")
129	        return loaded
130	    }
131	
132	    public func save(
133	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
134	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
135	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
136	        var values = try await load()
137	        if let metadata, !metadata.isEmpty {
138	            values[key] = metadata
139	        } else {
140	            values.removeValue(forKey: key)
141	        }
142	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist started host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(values.count, privacy: .public)")
143	        let persisted = try await save(values)
144	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist finished host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(persisted.count, privacy: .public)")
145	        return persisted
146	    }
147	
148	    public func save(
149	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
150	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
151	        let persistedValues = values.filter { !$0.value.isEmpty }
152	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist started entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
153	        try persist(persistedValues)
154	        cache = persistedValues
155	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist finished entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
156	        return persistedValues
157	    }
158	
159	    private func persist(_ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]) throws {
160	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
161	            at: fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent(),
162	            withIntermediateDirectories: true
163	        )
164	        let entries = values
165	            .map { Entry(key: $0.key, metadata: $0.value) }
166	            .sorted {
167	                [$0.key.hostID, $0.key.backendSessionID, $0.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
168	                    < [$1.key.hostID, $1.key.backendSessionID, $1.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
169	            }
170	        let data = try JSONEncoder().encode(entries)
171	        try data.write(to: fileURL, options: [.atomic])
172	    }
173	
174	    public static func defaultFileURL() -> URL {
175	        let directory = FileManager.default.urls(
176	            for: .applicationSupportDirectory,
177	            in: .userDomainMask
178	        ).first ?? FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
179	        return directory
180	            .appendingPathComponent("CodexDock", isDirectory: true)
181	            .appendingPathComponent("thread-metadata.json")
182	    }
183	}

383	    private func waitForDockRootCount(key: String, atLeast minimumCount: Int, timeout: TimeInterval) -> Bool {
384	        let root = element(id: AutomationID.Dock.root)
385	        let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(timeout)
386	        while Date() < deadline {
387	            if let count = semicolonValue(named: key, in: root.stringValue),
388	               count >= minimumCount {
389	                return true
390	            }
391	            RunLoop.current.run(until: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.25))
392	        }
393	        return false
394	    }

396	    private func semicolonValue(named key: String, in value: String) -> Int? {
397	        for segment in value.split(separator: ";") {
398	            let parts = segment.split(separator: "=", maxSplits: 1)
399	            guard parts.count == 2,
400	                  parts[0].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) == key else {
401	                continue
402	            }
403	            return Int(parts[1].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines))
404	        }
405	        return nil
406	    }

552	    func scrollUntilElementIsInComfortableSwipeArea(id: AutomationID, maxSwipes: Int) -> Bool {
553	        for _ in 0...maxSwipes {
554	            let candidate = element(id: id)
555	            if candidate.waitForExistence(timeout: 1), isVisibleForTap(candidate.frame) {
556	                if isComfortableSwipeFrame(candidate.frame) {
557	                    return true
558	                }
559	                if shouldScrollUp(toExpose: candidate.frame) {
560	                    swipeUp()
561	                } else {
562	                    swipeDown()
563	                }
564	            } else {
565	                swipeUp()
566	            }
567	        }
568	        return false
569	    }

577	    private func isComfortableSwipeFrame(_ frame: CGRect) -> Bool {
578	        let visibleFrame = primaryWindowFrame(defaultingTo: frame)
579	        let topInset: CGFloat = 96
580	        let bottomLimit = tabBars.firstMatch.exists
581	            ? tabBars.firstMatch.frame.minY - 12
582	            : visibleFrame.maxY - 96
583	        return frame.minY >= visibleFrame.minY + topInset
584	            && frame.maxY <= bottomLimit
585	    }
586	
587	    private func shouldScrollUp(toExpose frame: CGRect) -> Bool {
588	        frame.midY >= primaryWindowFrame(defaultingTo: frame).midY
589	    }
590	
591	    private func isVisibleForTap(_ frame: CGRect) -> Bool {
592	        guard frame.width > 1, frame.height > 1 else {
593	            return false
594	        }
595	        let visibleFrame = primaryWindowFrame(defaultingTo: frame)
596	        let bottomLimit = tabBars.firstMatch.exists
597	            ? tabBars.firstMatch.frame.minY - 1
598	            : visibleFrame.maxY - 1
599	        return frame.midY >= visibleFrame.minY + 1
600	            && frame.midY <= bottomLimit
601	            && frame.maxX > visibleFrame.minX
602	            && frame.minX < visibleFrame.maxX
603	    }
604	
605	    private func primaryWindowFrame(defaultingTo frame: CGRect) -> CGRect {
606	        let window = windows.firstMatch
607	        return window.exists ? window.frame : frame
608	    }

646	        while Date() < deadline {
647	            let rows = rowIDs.map { element(id: $0) }
648	            if rows.allSatisfy(\.exists) {
649	                let yPositions = rows.map { $0.frame.minY }
650	                if zip(yPositions, yPositions.dropFirst()).allSatisfy({ $0 <= $1 }) {
651	                    return true
652	                }
653	            }
654	            RunLoop.current.run(until: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.25))
655	        }

43	public struct AppServerReconnectPolicy: Sendable, Equatable {
44	    public let maxAttempts: Int
45	    public let initialDelayMilliseconds: Int
46	    public let maxDelayMilliseconds: Int
47	    public let jitterRatio: Double

49	    public init(
50	        maxAttempts: Int,
51	        initialDelayMilliseconds: Int,
52	        maxDelayMilliseconds: Int,
53	        jitterRatio: Double = 0.0
54	    ) {
55	        precondition(maxAttempts > 0, "Reconnect attempts must be positive")
56	        precondition(initialDelayMilliseconds >= 0, "Initial reconnect delay cannot be negative")
57	        precondition(maxDelayMilliseconds >= initialDelayMilliseconds, "Max reconnect delay must cover initial delay")
58	        precondition(jitterRatio >= 0, "Reconnect jitter cannot be negative")
59	        self.maxAttempts = maxAttempts
60	        self.initialDelayMilliseconds = initialDelayMilliseconds
61	        self.maxDelayMilliseconds = maxDelayMilliseconds
62	        self.jitterRatio = jitterRatio
63	    }
64	
65	    func delay(for attempt: Int) -> Duration {
66	        let exponent = max(0, min(attempt - 1, CodexDockConstants.AppServer.maximumBackoffExponent))
67	        let multiplier = 1 << exponent
68	        let baseDelay = min(maxDelayMilliseconds, initialDelayMilliseconds * multiplier)
69	        let jitterWindow = Int(Double(baseDelay) * jitterRatio)
70	        let jitter = jitterWindow > 0 ? Int.random(in: -jitterWindow...jitterWindow) : 0
71	        return .milliseconds(max(0, baseDelay + jitter))
72	    }
73	}

1	# Codex Dock Client
2	
3	This repo is the Swift client for the Codex Dock MVP.
4	
5	## App-Server Runbook
6	
7	There are two different app-server modes we need to keep separate.
8	
9	### 1. Normal daemon mode
10	
11	The Codex daemon is the normal local background service:
12	
13	```sh
14	rtk codex app-server daemon restart
15	rtk codex app-server daemon version
16	```
17	
18	Today, this daemon always starts its managed app-server on a Unix socket:
19	
20	```sh
21	app-server --remote-control --listen unix://
22	```
23	
24	That socket is:
25	
26	```text
27	/Users/aelaguiz/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock
28	```
29	
30	This is fine for local Codex tooling, but it is not reachable from an iPhone.
31	
32	### 2. Loopback WebSocket mode
33	
34	For local WebSocket development, start a direct app-server process in loopback
35	mode:
36	
37	```sh
38	rtk codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:4500
39	```
40	
41	Then the Swift test can point at:
42	
43	```sh
44	rtk env CODEX_DOCK_LOOPBACK_APP_SERVER_WS=ws://127.0.0.1:4500 swift test
45	```
46	
47	Important: loopback is only a local development step. It is not Phase 1
48	completion evidence, because an iPhone cannot use the Mac's `127.0.0.1`. The
49	phone-reachable acceptance test intentionally rejects loopback endpoints.
50	
51	After a loopback smoke run, stop the direct `codex app-server --listen
52	ws://127.0.0.1:4500` process and restart the normal daemon:
53	
54	```sh
55	rtk codex app-server daemon restart
56	```
57	
58	That restart restores the daemon's normal Unix-socket service. It does not move
59	the daemon itself into loopback WebSocket mode; current Codex daemon startup
60	does not expose that setting.
61	
62	### 3. Phone-reachable relay mode
63	
64	The raw Codex app-server still runs with bearer auth on the Mac. The iPhone does
65	not connect to that raw server directly. It connects to the Dock relay on the
66	Mac, and the relay uses the raw app-server token behind the scenes.
67	
68	```sh
69	rtk make services
70	```
71	
72	The phone-facing endpoint is:
73	
74	```text
75	<amir-m5-lan-or-tailscale-host>:4510
76	```
77	
78	For the personal LAN/Tailscale path, the relay accepts the iPhone without a
79	client bearer token. The relay advertises `_codexdock._tcp` with non-secret
80	Bonjour metadata so the app can find it after a normal home-screen launch.
81	
82	## Physical Phone Rule
83	
84	Mocks, scripted transports, Unix sockets, and loopback-only WebSockets do not
85	complete the physical phone path. The current phone path is the Dock relay on
86	`:4510`, with no iPhone-side bearer token. The iPhone 17 Pro uses
87	`ws://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` and
88	`ws://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`; the iPhone 14 uses
89	`ws://Amir-M5.local:4510` and `ws://192.168.50.74:4510`.
90	
91	Physical-device proof is Makefile-owned. Use `rtk make device-install` and
92	`rtk make device-config-verify`; if a phone is actively in use, unavailable, or
93	blocked by device tooling, record the exact skipped command and exact blocker.
94	Simulator, local relay, service-status, and generated-artifact proof only prove
95	the parts they actually exercise.
96	
97	## Exhaustive Sync Harness
98	
99	The repeatable over-time sync proof is documented in
100	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_RUNBOOK_2026-05-31.md`.
101	
102	Use it when checking whether Codex storage, app-server state, relay projection,
103	client-used routes, and the literal `iPhone 17` simulator display stay in sync.
104	The harness treats lag over the configured budget as a failure, even if a later
105	sample eventually catches up.
106	
107	## Canonical Service Start
108	
109	Use this target for local Dock development instead of manually starting and
110	stopping host services:
111	
112	```sh
113	rtk make services
114	```
115	
116	It starts/reuses two real services and leaves them running:
117	
118	- Raw Codex app-server on loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`
119	- Dock relay on `ws://<APP_SERVER_HOST>:4510`
120	
121	The raw app-server provides stored history. The relay is the app endpoint. Dock
122	Home subscribes to relay-owned `dock/*` methods: `dock/subscribe` returns the
123	first normalized snapshot, `dock/update` pushes deltas and heartbeats, and
124	`dock/resync` returns a replacement snapshot if the client detects a sequence
125	gap. The relay materializes app-server thread projections in SQLite at
126	`.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`, serves Dock Home from that state store, and
127	keeps stale rows visible when a source refresh fails.
128	
129	Card truth has one path. The relay may inspect raw app-server facts such as
130	`thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, live events, and live loaded
131	IDs internally, but Swift never uses those raw routes to prove Dock or Archive
132	cards. Swift renders card truth only from `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams.
133	
134	Row text has two separate meanings. Raw history `preview` is preserved as the
135	app-server's stored preview and may be the opening message. Dock overview rows
136	use relay-owned card fields from the canonical projection. That projection may
137	inspect newest turns and live events to compute honest activity, but any
138	unproven card makes the stream partial or stale instead of pretending the list
139	is fresh.
140	
141	The relay also owns OpenAI Realtime transcription. Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the
142	Mac environment or repo `.env`; the app never receives it. The default Realtime
143	transcription model is `gpt-realtime-whisper`, with optional Mac-side
144	`CODEX_DOCK_OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` and
145	`CODEX_DOCK_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_DELAY` overrides.
146	
147	The Dock filters loaded thread cards locally. It opens to `Newest`: one flat
148	newest-first list across configured hosts. Rows carry their own short host
149	name, repository or working directory, branch, status, last activity, local
150	label, and latest summary. `Host` and `Branch` are Dock lenses, not app-level
151	tabs or a separate sort picker; both preserve newest-first ordering inside
152	their groups. `Filters` opens one shared filter surface for host, branch,
153	canonical Dock status, repository or working directory, source, and the fixed
154	`Newest activity` sort. Status `Any` includes `Idle`, so idle rows are visible
155	by default and can be narrowed through the status filter. Search is full-width and
156	matches session title, label, repository or working directory, branch, summary,
157	status, host display name, host id, source, and thread id. Codex runtime
158	`notLoaded` is normalized by the relay to Dock `dormant`; Dock Home does not
159	spend row-badge space on that background state.
160	
161	The app has one root connectivity indicator. It appears above Dock and opens
162	the `System Health` sheet for relay and route diagnostics. Archive recovery,
163	cleanup, and relay host editing live in the Dock `More` menu as `Archived
164	Threads`, `Archive Cleanup`, and `Relay Settings` task sheets, not app-level
165	tabs. The labels are `Unconfigured`,
166	`Checking`, `Online`, `Partial`, `Reconnecting`, `Backgrounded`, `Resuming`,
167	`Stale`, `Offline`, `Error`, and `Config error`. A nil host bearer token is
168	normal for the personal physical-phone relay path; it is not shown as missing
169	credentials.
170	
171	Live Session detail connections reconnect automatically when recovery is safe.
172	Swift consumes relay-owned `thread/detail/subscribe`, `thread/detail/update`,
173	and `thread/detail/resync` projection rows. The relay may still use raw
174	`thread/read includeTurns:false`, paged `thread/turns/list`, and upstream
175	`thread/resume excludeTurns:true` internally, but those raw routes are not the
176	phone-facing Thread Detail display contract. Failed user sends are not silently
177	replayed. If the relay loses its upstream session, it either re-resumes upstream
178	or closes the phone WebSocket so Swift can mark the detail stale or reconnect.
179	
180	When iOS backgrounds the app, root refresh and reconnect attempts pause instead
181	of spending retry budget. Open details keep visible events, request action
182	state, and draft text but are no longer labeled fresh. Active voice capture is
183	cancelled without auto-submitting. On foreground resume, Dock and Archive
184	refresh from root, open details rehydrate through `thread/detail/resync`, and
185	the indicator moves through `Backgrounded` / `Resuming` / `Reconnecting` as
186	appropriate.
187	
188	The service targets install per-repo launchd files on macOS and systemd user
189	files on Linux, with runtime files under `.codex-dock/`:
190	
191	```text
192	.codex-dock/services/com.aelaguiz.codex-dock.app-server.plist
193	.codex-dock/services/com.aelaguiz.codex-dock.relay.plist
194	.codex-dock/services/codex-dock-app-server.service
195	.codex-dock/services/codex-dock-relay.service
196	.codex-dock/app-server.token
197	.codex-dock/service.env
198	.codex-dock/host.env
199	.codex-dock/logs/app-server.log
200	.codex-dock/logs/app-server.err.log
201	.codex-dock/logs/dock-relay.log
202	.codex-dock/logs/dock-relay.err.log
203	```
204	
205	The default app endpoint is:
206	
207	```text
208	ws://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510
209	```
210	
211	Check services without restarting:
212	
213	```sh
214	rtk make app-server-status
215	rtk make dock-relay-status
216	```
217	
218	Process health, route health, and card freshness are separate. `/readyz` only
219	means the relay process can answer HTTP. `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`,
220	and `/syncz` expose process and route health only; they do not prove Dock or
221	Archive card ordering, contents, freshness, completeness, or membership.
222	
223	Route-health diagnostics:

227	rtk make relay-host-compare HOSTS=amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510,home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510
228	rtk make relay-debug-bundle
229	```
230	
231	The relay stores bounded route evidence under `.codex-dock/observability/`.
232	Automatic probes only use auto-probe-safe routes; archive, turn, and
233	transcription routes are passive evidence from real app traffic. HTTP
234	diagnostics intentionally do not expose card rows or stored card state.
235	
236	Print the app-safe host config plus raw dev smoke helpers:

249	Normal verification should use `rtk make services`, `rtk make
